(b) closed event error/warning codes and total error precedence; (c) R002/R003 locally motivated preparation eligibility, catalog-only all-null/no-action/nontrusted/null-money behavior, candidate-associated all-non-null binding, cross-candidate rejection, coordinator no-event and event-backed `not_offered`, `verification_status: verified`, exact source/freshness correlation, the exact **Eligible to earn on qualifying settled requests** conditional verdict, exact operator-owned local/trusted copy, and economics/demand separation; (d) worker-only event sequencing plus the exact bounded cancellation-ack schema, request echo, six outcomes including `busy`, the 2.000-second monotonic cancel-lock deadline, total acquired-lock outcome precedence, nullability, exit/mutation/resource rules, marker-race semantics, and cancel-process read/marker-only authority; (e) the versioned projection/action/accounting contract for `cleanup_published_artifact`, bounded `cleanup_targets` with immutable `event_model_key`, managed-v3 totals, configured-legacy protected totals, logical-byte accounting, truthful APFS copy, and exact budget policy; (f) published and staging continuous `cancel.lock` ownership from final marker check through rename, both parent barriers, durable readback-validated `tombstoned`, reversible post-crash precommit restoration, and operation/cleanup/cancel recovery ownership; ./docs/product-roadmap/build-1/reservation-rebaseline-plan-v8.md:217:3. The proposed acknowledgement is a single JSON object capped at 4096 bytes with exact fields `schema`, `transaction_id`, nullable `attempt_id`, `outcome`, and `observed_at`; `schema` is `model_catalog_transaction_cancel_ack.v1`, and `transaction_id` must byte-for-byte echo the syntactically valid requested ID. The closed `outcome` values are `recorded`, `already_recorded`, `terminal`, `not_active`, `stale`, and `busy`.
./docs/product-roadmap/build-1/reservation-rebaseline-plan-v8.md:268:Inventory enumerates only `.macprovider-prepared-v3/objects`, capped at 256 exact receipts. The v2 projection also carries a required closed top-level `cleanup_targets` array with at most 256 entries, deterministically ordered by lowercase `artifact_identity_digest`. It contains every verified managed v3 identity observed by the bounded inventory, including objects with no current catalog row. Each entry has exactly `artifact_identity_digest`, `display_model_id`, `model_revision`, `artifact_id`, `release_id`, required immutable `event_model_key`, nullable current `model_key`, `root_identity_digest`, `receipt_sha256`, exact logical `estimated_bytes`, `keep_set_status`, nullable `protected_reason`, and `cleanup`. `event_model_key` is copied from the historical model key sealed into the publication receipt and is durably copied into the cleanup reservation/active/deletion records; every cleanup event uses it as the retained event schema's non-null `model_key`. The nullable current `model_key` remains only the present catalog match and may be null for an orphan. The two digests are lowercase 64-hex; `keep_set_status` is `protected` or `reclaimable`; `protected_reason` is required exactly for `protected`; and `cleanup` uses the v2 action shape. A reclaimable entry has one available `cleanup_published_artifact` action carrying the same artifact digest, event key, and bytes; a protected entry has an unavailable action and exact reason. Missing/stale receipt identity, malformed inventory, or overflow makes the array empty/unavailable with the storage totals and actions fail closed. Row cleanup actions, if retained, must be identical projections of the corresponding top-level entry; absence from the current signed catalog never makes a reclaimable v3 identity unreachable. The operator patch must approve these exact fields/enums or an equivalently closed bounded target contract before implementation.

specs/SPEC-044-malibu-model-catalog-economics.md:102:**SPEC-044-R002 - Versioned row schema.** The CLI projection MUST emit a closed, versioned JSON envelope with `schema: "model_catalog_economics.v1"`, a wall-clock RFC3339 `generated_at`, a monotonic unsigned integer `projection_sequence`, a `source` object identifying the CLI build and feed provenance, an array of rows, and a projection-level `warnings` array. The v1 `source` object MUST include `cli_version`, `cli_build_commit`, `process_launch_id`, `process_started_at`, `projection_protocol_version`, `rate_card_source`, nullable `rate_card_digest`, nullable `rate_card_signature_digest`, nullable `demand_feed_digest`, nullable `candidate_feed_digest`, and `rate_card_max_age_seconds`; `process_launch_id` MUST be a lowercase hyphen-separated UUID v4 string generated fresh on CLI process start from at least 128 bits of CSPRNG entropy and MUST NOT be derivable from a PID, host serial, MAC address, host UUID, provider id, wallet, username, or any other hardware or identity value. `source.rate_card_source` MUST use the same closed enum as row `rate_source`: `live_signed`, `static_signed`, or `none`. `projection_sequence` MUST increase within a single CLI process for each newly generated projection and MAY reset after CLI restart; callers MUST use it only to order projections that have the same `source.process_launch_id`. When Malibu observes a new `source.process_launch_id`, it MUST treat the projection as a new CLI session, reset its ordering baseline, discard older in-flight projection ordering comparisons, and show a brief reconnecting or refreshing state before rendering the new projection. Each row MUST include model identity (`model_key`, `served_model_id`, `display_model_id`, nullable `action_model_id`), local state (`is_current`, `weights_present_locally`, `runtime_state`, nullable `estimated_gb`, `fit`, nullable `disabled_reason`, `warning_codes`), admission state (`admission`), economics (nullable `rate_card_version`, nullable `rate_card_generated_at`, nullable `rate_card_key`, `rate_source`, nullable `prompt_rate_usd_per_million_tokens`, nullable `completion_rate_usd_per_million_tokens`, nullable `provider_share_bps`, nullable `provider_prompt_payout_usd_per_million_tokens`, nullable `provider_completion_payout_usd_per_million_tokens`, `economics_state`), demand signals (nullable `demand_rank`, nullable `demand_weight`, nullable `ready_provider_count`, nullable `supply_deficit_score`), and actions (`switch`, `prepare`, `evaluate`, `adopt_recommendation`, `cleanup_staging`) as explicit objects with `available`, `requires_confirmation`, nullable `transaction_kind`, nullable `transaction_id`, nullable `action_timeout_seconds`, nullable `estimated_bytes`, and nullable `unavailable_reason`. The row `admission` object MUST include `state`, `source`, nullable `coordinator_event_id`, nullable `state_observed_at`, `catalog_economics_permitted`, and `settlement_capable`; `source` is `local_default` or `coordinator`, `state` MUST use the SPEC-046/SPEC-047 admission-state enum, `source: "local_default"` permits only `local_only`, `not_offered`, or `offerable` and MUST set `catalog_economics_permitted: false` and `settlement_capable: false`, `source: "coordinator"` permits only SPEC-047 coordinator states, `catalog_economics_permitted` MAY be true only when `source: "coordinator"` and `state` is `catalog_priced` or `settlement_capable`, and `settlement_capable` MAY be true only when `source: "coordinator"` and `state` is `settlement_capable`. Rows whose `admission` object is missing, malformed, stale relative to the signed rate-card evidence, or inconsistent with SPEC-047 MUST set `economics_state` to `blocked` or `unavailable`, null all money-facing payout fields, and make money-motivated actions unavailable. Row `warning_codes` MUST be an array of closed warning-code enum values that apply to that specific row; the top-level `warnings` array applies to the projection as a whole. `economics_state: "trusted"` MUST include non-null rate-card identity, provider-share, and prompt/completion catalog and payout fields, and MUST require `admission.catalog_economics_permitted: true`; Malibu MUST NOT render earning-eligible, settlement-ready, or paid-routing copy unless `admission.settlement_capable: true`. Rows with `rate_source: "none"` or `economics_state: "unavailable"` MUST set rate-card identity and all rate/payout numeric fields to null rather than placeholder zero values. Rows with `economics_state: "blocked"` MUST set money-facing rate/payout fields to null unless the CLI can still identify a verified signed rate card while blocking actions for a non-rate reason; Malibu MUST hide economics copy for blocked rows unless `economics_state` is `trusted`. Rows with `economics_state: "fallback"` or `"stale"` MAY include the signed/static/stale rate fields only as disabled warning context and MUST NOT render them as actionable trusted economics. For an available action, `transaction_kind`, `transaction_id`, and `action_timeout_seconds` MUST be non-null; `action_timeout_seconds` MUST be greater than zero and MUST NOT exceed 1800 seconds. For available `switch_model`, `prepare_model`, `switch_model_deferred`, `cleanup_staging`, `adopt_recommendation`, and any `evaluate_model` action with non-null `estimated_bytes` or `action_timeout_seconds` greater than 10 seconds, `requires_confirmation` MUST be true, and Malibu MUST enforce confirmation for those transaction kinds even if a malformed projection sets the flag false. For an unavailable action, `transaction_kind`, `transaction_id`, and `action_timeout_seconds` MUST be null. A row's `rate_source` MUST be equal to `source.rate_card_source` unless the row uses a more conservative value, where `none` is more conservative than `static_signed`, and `static_signed` is more conservative than `live_signed`. Closed v1 enum values are: `runtime_state` = `current`, `ready`, `catalog`, `needs_preparation`, `blocked`; `fit` = `fits`, `does_not_fit`, `unknown`; admission `source` = `local_default`, `coordinator`; admission `state` = `local_only`, `not_offered`, `offerable`, `offer_submitted`, `offer_rejected`, `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `settlement_capable`, `withdrawn`, `revoked`; `rate_source` = `live_signed`, `static_signed`, `none`; `economics_state` = `trusted`, `fallback`, `stale`, `blocked`, `unavailable`; warning codes = `feed_fallback`, `feed_stale`, `feed_signature_invalid`, `feed_generation_mismatch`, `rate_multiplier_unknown`, `model_not_local`, `model_not_supported`, `hardware_fit_unknown`, `hardware_does_not_fit`, `admission_state_missing`, `admission_state_not_settlement_capable`, `warm_swap_unavailable`, `action_unavailable`, `old_cli_fallback`, `projection_unavailable`, `projection_timeout`, `staging_cleanup_required`; action `transaction_kind` = `switch_model`, `switch_model_deferred`, `prepare_model`, `evaluate_model`, `adopt_recommendation`, `cleanup_staging`, or null when unavailable. The v1 transaction event stream MUST use a closed JSON-lines envelope with `schema: "model_catalog_transaction_event.v1"`, matching `transaction_id`, matching `transaction_kind`, `model_key`, monotonic per-transaction `event_sequence`, RFC3339 `emitted_at`, `state`, nullable `progress`, nullable `error_code`, and nullable `warning_code`. Closed event `state` values are `queued`, `running`, `cancel_requested`, `cancelled`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `timed_out`; `progress`, when present, MUST include a localized-safe `stage_label_key` and at least one of `bytes_completed`/nullable `bytes_expected`, `percent_complete`, or `heartbeat`. Cancellation MUST be requested through the same CLI-owned transaction interface, MUST produce either `cancel_requested` followed by `cancelled` or a terminal `succeeded`/`failed` if the commit point has already passed, and MUST never require Malibu to kill the CLI process or delete files directly. Unknown enum values, unknown action transaction kinds, malformed event envelopes, or event transaction mismatches MUST make the affected row or transaction non-actionable and show a generic unsupported warning; they MUST NOT make Malibu reject the whole projection unless the projection envelope schema itself is unsupported.

specs/SPEC-023-installer-autotune-recommend.md:152:  8. **Activation, identity, and aggregation are pinned to what today's fleet and today's sibling specs actually accept.** New §3.7.8 defines the feed's `release.json` binding, the release-ledger feed-set evolution rule (three historical sets stay permanently valid; a fourth artifact-bound five-feed set is added and becomes mandatory from the activation release), and a §12.2-style **two-stage activation**: at Stage A the feed is generated, signed, served, baked, release-bound, and ledger-recorded but is NOT added to the compatibility-set manifest's exact nine-name `components.catalog.files` map, so a v0.10 payload installs on every already-shipped updater; Stage B may widen that map only after a bridge CLI has shipped stable AND previous-stable is at or after it. §3.7.4 adds a **closed artifact-identity matrix** binding `runtime_format` to its only legal `hash_algorithm`, `source_ref.kind`, and `allowed_runtime_sources` set, so an individually schema-valid but semantically inconsistent tuple is an integrity failure at generation and consumption. §3.7.4, §3.7.7, §13 Q14, AC-CAT-7, AC-CAT-17, and the SPEC-047-R003 amendment restrict `catalog_priced`/`settlement_capable`, the SPEC-010 wire pair, and SPEC-022 settlement bindings to the **primary artifact only** — a secondary MLX quantization is excluded on the same SPEC-010-R001/R004 ground as a GGUF artifact — so v0.10.0 is strictly consistent with SPEC-010 as it stands and needs no SPEC-010 amendment *(historical: lifted in v0.10.3 by SPEC-010 v1.7 R007)*. §3.3.1 removes `provider_share_bps`/`global_multiplier_ppm` from class rows (they are release-global values that the coordinator's `rewards.rate_card` rows cannot represent), states the exact JSON-to-YAML field mapping, and adds a generated-feed / billing-config parity release gate. §16.2(a) replaces exact-top-N semantics with one complete bounded model — a named Space-Saving summary with deterministic eviction, conservative-lower-bound floor semantics, saturating overflow counters, and opaque window-scoped HMAC principal tokens bounded per bucket — with `INTAKE_UNKNOWN_PRINCIPALS_PER_BUCKET` and `INTAKE_UNKNOWN_KEY_DISTINCT_CAP` added to §16.4. §3.7.6 makes a stale feed fail artifact-derived capability while staying selectable for diagnostics/fallback provenance, §12.2(b)(ii) narrows the `listed` prohibition to paid and default routing while keeping `omlx_seeded` rows fully local-only, and §3.2 states what `candidate` staging does and does not authorize.
specs/SPEC-023-installer-autotune-recommend.md:512:- `verified_provider_matrix` is the canonical provenance value denoting a gate recomputed solely from `N` verified provider autotune measurements on eligible hardware (§12 promotion). It is the required value a row promoted away from `omlx_seeded` MUST carry (§5, §12). Unlike `measured_single_host` (one host) or `runtime_validated_only` (no trusted throughput gate), it denotes the verified-provider matrix that is the sole promotion/admission authority for a formerly provisional row. It is RESERVED and inert in Stage 1: any newly created or modified row carrying `verified_provider_matrix` MUST be rejected at catalog authoring, lint, and signing until the Stage-2 evidence binding ships (§12.4, AC-OMLX-12).
specs/SPEC-023-installer-autotune-recommend.md:1009:- `primary_artifact_id` MUST name an entry in that model's `artifacts` map whose `runtime_format` is `mlx_safetensors`, and that entry's `source_ref.repo_id`, `source_ref.revision`, `hash_algorithm`, and `hash` MUST correspond to the candidate row's `model_id`, `model_revision`, `macprovider.snapshot-manifest.v1`, and `model_sha256` respectively. **The `verified` requirement on that entry is scoped by the row's `runtime_status`.** For a candidate-catalog row entering or held at `listed` or `recommendable`, the primary artifact's `verification_status` MUST be `verified` (§3.7.5, §16.1 P1). For a `candidate` row it MAY remain `declared` — that is exactly what operator staging means (§3.2) — but the entry MUST still be schema-valid and identity-corresponding as stated above: staging permits an unconfirmed hash, never an unnamed, absent, or mismatched primary artifact.

Derived from coordinator admission events, aggregated only: no provider id, pseudonym, hardware fingerprint, or per-provider row may appear in the intake record. Offers from providers under an active route, trust, payout, or registration sanction MUST be excluded (SPEC-047-R009, the aggregate authority; SPEC-047-R007 for the offer path). **[v0.10.4]** "Under an active route, trust, payout, or registration sanction" is DEFINED, for this signal, by the SPEC-047 v0.1.6 closed current-state predicate `provider_intake_sanctioned(provider_id, at)` — route: admission rejection or canary sanction; trust: no active hardware-trust root; payout: vacuous until SPEC-016 defines a per-provider payout sanction; registration: a revoked provider token with no active token — evaluated at the aggregate's build time, so a provider sanctioned after offering is excluded with every offer it recorded. The count MUST be reported as **suppressed** below the effective k-anonymity floor — `INTAKE_K_ANONYMITY_MIN` (§16.4, default `3`) — so a two-provider interest cannot be read back as an identification of those providers. `INTAKE_K_ANONYMITY_MIN` is **owned by SPEC-023**, not borrowed from SPEC-017: it is the minimum that applies to BOTH this signal and the §16.2(a) `unmatched_model_request_count` signal. SPEC-017 MAY select a HIGHER floor for the signal it owns and MUST NOT select a lower one (§16.7); it never lowers the floor applied here.

specs/SPEC-031-canary-degrade-sanctions.md:820:| FR-CAN22 sole-provider floor | **Implemented** (v0.2) | `RecordCanaryResult` spares the **sole buyer-serving provider** on **any** canary-only signal: it returns `CanaryTripFloorHeld` (no state change, keeps accruing the counter) instead of degrading/banning, and the caller emits `canary_floor_held` / `pool_redundancy_low` redundancy telemetry (`hasOtherBuyerServingForModelLocked`). The **injected predicate** (`canaryBuyerServing`) applies the coordinator's **request-independent** routability gates: `RoutingEligible` (state ready AND `SlotsFree>0` AND auth/catalog/receipt gates) AND transport-reachable (a WS-tunneled peer needs a live stored session; else a non-empty `EndpointURL`) AND `MaxContextTokens>0` (sanity, excludes the degenerate zero) AND not Tier-2-excluded (hash/encryption/attestation), keyed on the **active** model (case-folded `ModelID`, not declared-but-cold `SupportedModels`). Excluded: declared-only, degraded, Tier-2-excluded, **busy** (`SlotsFree==0`), **negative** free slots, and transport-unreachable (`HTTPForwardingOnly` with no endpoint) peers. Excluding a genuinely-busy real peer is **over-protective** — the safe direction; it re-counts when a slot frees. **Request-DEPENDENT eligibility is deliberately NOT evaluated** and cannot be, because the floor runs without a request in hand: per-request **context sufficiency** (`MaxContextTokens ≥ the request's token estimate`, so a peer advertising a tiny positive window like 1 passes yet is filtered per request) and **provisional quota** (checking `admission.CheckQuota` under `pool.mu` would couple the registry lock to the admission-DB mutex — an availability convoy). A same-model peer that passes the request-independent gates but is filtered per-request (tiny context, exhausted quota) can therefore still lift the floor, and — because buyer routing **skips** such a peer *without* recording an FR-P11a breaker fault — the breaker is not a universal backstop for that case. **This is not a regression:** the floor only ever *spares* a provider the pre-floor canary would have removed; it never removes one the old code kept, so the adversarial-peer empty-pool outcome is *identical to the pre-floor baseline*. Adversarial-safe multi-provider peer-genuineness (full request-aware / coordinator-observed-serving eligibility) is **deferred to FR-CAN23**, with no current-prod impact (single provider, canary disabled). Applies to both tiers (precedes the tier branch). Removing a sole provider still requires evidence independent of the canary — the FR-P11a buyer-path breaker (on real failing requests), a confirmed transport death, or item-9 weight evidence. |
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:107:**[amended v0.1.5]** The authorized actor `coordinator admission policy` acts, for OPERATOR-origin decisions to `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `settlement_capable`, and `revoked`, through exactly one production caller: an **operator decision request** `POST /admin/model-admission/decisions`. **Credential and attribution.** The request is authenticated with the per-actor coordinator operator credential class (`auth.operator_keys`, the class the `/admin` trust-granting surfaces use, which yields an operator actor id) — never the shared single-value `operator_key` — and the appended event's `actor` is `operator:<actor id>` (grammar `^operator:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`). The `settlement_capable` edge, the money-path grant, is **dual-control** exactly as `/admin/hardware-trust/approve` is: the request appends NO event: after steps (1)–(4) below succeed it durably records a pending decision (`pending_decision_id`, grammar `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`; the request's canonical body digest; the evaluated head; `requested_by`; `created_at`; a 24-hour expiry) and answers `model_admission_decision.v1` with the pending values: `previous_admission_state` and `admission_state` both the unchanged current state, `reason_code` the request's reason, `coordinator_event_id` the evaluated head, `accepted_at` the pending record's creation time, `decided_by` the requesting actor, `replayed` false, `pending_decision_id` set, `bound_member` null; a replay of that request answers the same pending record (`replayed: true`); a pending record is consumed by exactly one approval, expires unused, and is invalidated by any event appended for the candidate. `POST /admin/model-admission/decisions/<pending_decision_id>/approve` with request schema `model_admission_decision_approve_request.v1` (exactly `schema`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `pending_decision_id`, `expected_coordinator_event_id`, `idempotency_key`; same grammars) by a DISTINCT operator actor (the same actor is `dual_control_required`; when fewer than two distinct operator actors are configured, the initial `settlement_capable` request itself is refused synchronously with `dual_control_unavailable` and no pending record is created) commits the append under this approval precedence, executed as one unit inside the provider's section: (a) the path and body `pending_decision_id` MUST be equal and the body's `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, and `expected_coordinator_event_id` MUST equal the pending record's stored values, else `invalid_request`; (b) approval idempotency — the approval body is canonicalized and digested under (`pending_decision_id`, `idempotency_key`): an identical digest answers the committed response (`replayed: true`), a different digest under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`, both before any pending or head check — and because the closed approval body carries nothing but the bound fields and the key, every divergent body under a reused key is a bound-field disagreement already answered by (a), so (a) precedes (b) and `idempotency_conflict` on an approval is defence in depth; (c) pending status — consumed `pending_consumed`, expired `pending_expired`, invalidated or unknown `no_pending_decision`; (d) distinct actor, else `dual_control_required`; (e) the candidate's current head MUST still equal the pending record's evaluated head, else `stale_head` and the record is invalidated; (f) the SPEC-047-R003 preconditions re-evaluated in full; (g) release-generation re-compare and append; an unknown or invalidated id is `no_pending_decision`, an expired one `pending_expired`, a consumed one `pending_consumed`; approvals replay in their own namespace (`pending_decision_id`, `idempotency_key`): an identical-key retry of a committed approval answers the original committed response with `replayed: true`, whatever happened since; a distinct-key approval of a consumed record is `pending_consumed`; two concurrent distinct-key approvals resolve, under the section, as one append and one `pending_consumed`. The other four edges commit on the request. **Bounds.** The request is bounded by payload size and parser work like every SPEC-047-R007 mutation and rate-limited per operator credential and source address; it MUST NOT draw on any per-provider rate window, so a provider cannot exhaust an operator's ability to append a decision for its own candidates. **Request schema** `model_admission_decision_request.v1`, fields exactly `schema`, `provider_id` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`), `candidate_id` (`^byom_[a-z2-7]{52}$`), `next_state` (one of the five), `reason_code` (`^operator_[a-z0-9_]{2,56}$` — the `operator_` prefix is the operator origin's reserved namespace), `expected_coordinator_event_id` (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`), and `idempotency_key` (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`); unknown fields are rejected before any state transition. **Precedence**, executed as one unit inside the provider's decision critical section (below): (1) idempotency — the request is canonicalized and keyed by (`provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `idempotency_key`) (the store's replay index is extended to that triple); an identical canonical request answers with the result it originally produced — the appended event, or the pending decision — whatever the current head, marked `replayed: true`; the same key with a different body fails closed (`idempotency_conflict`); two concurrent first-seen requests with one key resolve as one append plus one replay or one append plus one conflict, never `stale_head`; (2) head compare — `expected_coordinator_event_id` must equal the candidate's current head, else `stale_head`; (3) edge validation against this table from the latest state, else `invalid_transition`; (4) for `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable` only, the SPEC-047-R003 preconditions in their stated order, each with its own code (the other three edges skip this step); (5) under the release read lock (below), the release-generation re-compare and the append as one unit; the appended event records `evaluated_release_generation`. The first failure wins and nothing is appended. **Head and event ids.** `coordinator_event_id` is unique per (`provider_id`, `candidate_id`) — the store's `UNIQUE(provider_id, request_id)` plus the event's own content digest — and the head is the event with the highest append sequence for that candidate, never a content comparison. **Response schema** `model_admission_decision.v1`, exactly `schema`, `generated_at`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `previous_admission_state`, `admission_state`, `reason_code`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, `decided_by` (the actor id), `replayed`, nullable `pending_decision_id`, and — non-null exactly for a committed `settlement_capable` — `bound_member` (`source`, nullable `artifact_id`, `hash_algorithm`, `hash`). `model_admission_status.v1` (SPEC-047-R002) keeps its exact field set; its value semantics change in one place, stated in R002. **Transition origins and reason sets are closed and disjoint:** the operator origin appends only the five edges above with `operator_`-prefixed reasons; the offer path appends `offer_submitted` with `provider_offer_submitted`; the withdrawal path appends `withdrawn` with the SPEC-047-R002 withdrawal enum; the synthetic-probe path appends `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, or `revoked` with `synthetic_probe_`-prefixed reasons; the drift path appends `revoked` with exactly one of `runtime_identity_drift`, `catalog_artifact_feed_changed`, `catalog_row_changed`, `catalog_row_ineligible`, `catalog_runtime_source_disallowed`, `receipt_key_unavailable`. Each origin emits only its own REASON set (three target states have two origins); a reason from another origin's set is `invalid_request`. `offer_rejected` is unreachable in v0.1.5: offer validation rejects synchronously (HTTP 4xx, closed code, nothing appended) and no origin appends that edge; the table row stays for a later validator lane, and the R008 rejected-offer cases are stated in terms of synchronous rejection. **Decision critical section.** It is scoped per `provider_id`: every decision and approval, drift event, session-to-candidate binding derivation or mutation (SPEC-047-R003 — whose uniqueness predicate spans all of a provider's candidates), and reload-sweep step for any of the provider's candidates takes that provider's section, and a section is never taken while the provider-registry lock is held (lock order: section, then registry). The provider's section also owns a monotonic **binding generation**, incremented under the section, in the same critical region as the append itself, on every event appended for any of the provider's candidates and on every binding mutation. **Release lock and generation.** The coordinator holds one release read-write lock over ONE immutable release snapshot — the candidate catalog, the compatible-previous catalogs, the artifact feeds and every per-release identity set, the Tier-2 catalog material, and the generation. A reload stages all of them and then takes the WRITE side to swap the whole snapshot and publish its monotonic generation as one act; no part of a release is ever visible before the others. Decisions and approvals take the READ side across the WHOLE evaluation — steps (1)–(5), including every R003 read of catalog rows, identity sets, runtime-source policy, and Tier-2 material — offer-time matching takes it across the match, session identity verification takes it across the verdict, and route-time snapshot creation takes it across the compare-and-insert. **Every append origin takes the provider section**: the offer path, the offer validator, the withdrawal path, the synthetic-probe path, the operator path, and the drift path each acquire the provider's section BEFORE reading candidate state and hold it through the event append, the invalidation of pending decisions for that candidate, the binding-generation increment, and the binding refresh or clear — one linearization point, so no route attempt can observe a candidate set the append has already changed. After publication the R006 sweeps take each provider's section in turn and stamp every surviving `catalog_priced`/`settlement_capable` candidate's binding with `validated_release_generation` = the new generation (a candidate the sweep has not yet reached is unroutable, not revoked). BYOM route-time snapshot creation (SPEC-047-R003) takes no provider section: under the release read lock it is an atomic compare-and-insert that re-reads, immediately before the insert, the candidate's head, the session binding and its `bound_coordinator_event_id`, the provider's binding generation captured at evaluation, and requires the binding's `validated_release_generation` to equal the published release generation; any difference fails the attempt closed. **Offer listing.** An operator decides on recorded state, never on a provider's claim: `GET /admin/model-admission/offers?provider_id=<id>` (same credential class; `provider_id` validated by its grammar, any other query parameter rejected) answers `model_admission_offer_list.v1`, exactly `schema`, `generated_at`, `provider_id`, `candidates` — ordered by `candidate_id`, bounded by the per-provider candidate cap — each item exactly `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, `runtime_source` (persisted on the offer event from v0.1.5), `admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `state_observed_at`, `reason_code`, `catalog_match_state`, `catalog_match_reason`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, nullable `catalog_row_model_id`, nullable `catalog_row_model_sha256`, nullable `catalog_release_id`, nullable `catalog_candidate_sha256`, nullable `catalog_signer_key_id`, `catalog_members` (at most 16 tagged members, each exactly `source`, `hash_algorithm`, `hash`, and nullable `artifact_id`, `artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, `artifact_candidate_catalog_sha256` — null exactly when `source` is `candidate_row`), `last_event_actor`, and `session` (nullable: `bound`, `bound_coordinator_event_id`, `validated_release_generation`, `verified_member` as a member record or null, `receipt_key_present`, `catalog_release_id`) — the live-session facts R003(iv) will evaluate; the actor of every event (drift included) is readable here, while `model_admission_status.v1` exposes the reason only. A decision request for a candidate with no offer fails closed (`no_offer`). **Errors** on all three endpoints use the existing `{"error":{"code","message"}}` envelope with exactly: `invalid_operator_token` (401), `invalid_request` (400), `no_offer` (404), `stale_head`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_transition`, `catalog_match_required`, `catalog_match_stale`, `catalog_row_not_recommendable`, `catalog_material_unavailable`, `no_verified_session`, `dual_control_required`, `dual_control_unavailable`, `no_pending_decision`, `pending_expired`, `pending_consumed`, `runtime_source_not_allowed` (all 409), and `rate_limited` (429).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:126:`schema` is that literal; `nonce` is 32 lowercase hex characters drawn from a cryptographically secure source at every build, so the SHA-256 the SPEC-023 §16.8 manifest records identifies ONE build even when two builds carry identical rows and the same second (the retained file is one read of one build, never a byte-equal replay of an earlier one); `generated_at`, `window_start`, and `window_end` are RFC3339 UTC timestamps with second precision in the one form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, `window_end == generated_at` and `window_start == generated_at − 30 days` exactly; `k_anonymity_min` is the integer `3` — SPEC-023 v0.10.4 §16.4 fixes `INTAKE_K_ANONYMITY_MIN` at 3 for that revision, and a different floor requires a lockstep amendment of SPEC-023, SPEC-017, and this SPEC; `rows` is an array ordered by `catalog_model_key` ascending (UTF-8 bytes) with no repeated key, each element exactly `catalog_model_key` (a SPEC-023 §3.2 normalized catalog key, `[a-z0-9._/-]{1,128}`), `distinct_provider_offer_count` (an integer ≥ `k_anonymity_min`, or `null`), and `suppressed` (a boolean; `true` exactly when the count is `null`). **Materialized snapshot, not a per-request scan.** The coordinator builds the aggregate on a fixed cadence — every 15 minutes, and once at startup — as one bounded job: one indexed scan of `offer_submitted` events with coordinator `created_at_utc` in the window (the store's admission-event table indexes `(state, created_at_utc)`), under a query timeout of 10 seconds and a hard ceiling of 100 000 DISTINCT `(provider_id, intake_model_key)` pairs; a job that exceeds either, or that cannot read every sanction source below, produces NO snapshot and leaves the previous one in place. **Consistency.** The build reads the offer events first, as one scan, and then evaluates the sanction predicate once per counted provider; the snapshot therefore reflects offers as of `generated_at` and sanctions as of a moment at or after it, which is monotone in the safe direction — a sanction applied during the build is honoured, a sanction lifted during it shows at the next build — and no partial snapshot is ever published (the snapshot pointer is swapped once, after every provider is evaluated). `GET` reads the current snapshot only (constant work per request; it is still rate-limited per operator credential and source address like the other operator endpoints and appends nothing) and answers `intake_unavailable` (503) when no snapshot exists, the newest is older than two cadences (30 minutes), or the newest is dated in the future (a clock step never serves a snapshot as current); `generated_at` is the snapshot's build time. **Window anchor.** Membership is decided by the event's coordinator-assigned append time — the admission-event row's `created_at_utc` column, set by the coordinator when it appends the event — never by any provider-signed timestamp in the offer package. **Counting rule.** A provider counts once for catalog key `K` when at least one `offer_submitted` event appended for that provider by the offer path with `created_at_utc` in `[window_start, window_end]` carries `intake_model_key == K`. `intake_model_key` is recorded on the offer event AT OFFER TIME by a resolution that is DISTINCT from the v0.1.5 `catalog_match_state`: the signed `artifact_hashes` of the offer are resolved against EVERY row of the current admitted release's candidate catalog by primary digest (`candidate`, `watch`, `listed`, and `recommendable` rows alike — the point of the signal is supply for keys the catalog has NOT admitted, which the v0.1.5 match, restricted to `listed`/`recommendable` rows, can never name) and against the release's usable identity set of verified artifacts; a pair that resolves to more than one row, or pairs that span two keys, resolve to no key. The provider-asserted `catalog_model_key` and `served_model_ref` are never read. An offer whose hashes resolve to no key carries an empty `intake_model_key` and counts for none. The offer's `catalog_match_state` is irrelevant to counting: a `catalog_matched` offer for a listed key counts toward that key (existing supply is still supply), and an `unmatched` offer for a `candidate` row counts toward that row's key. Later withdrawal, revocation, or drift does not un-count an offer (the signal is recorded interest, not current state); a provider offering `K` from several candidates counts once. The scan is over DISTINCT `(provider_id, intake_model_key)` pairs of the window — bounded by providers × keys, never by event volume — and the ceiling below applies to pairs and is enforced AT THE STORE: the store reads at most ceiling + 1 pairs (a SQL `LIMIT`; the in-memory store stops appending), so the build fails closed on the ceiling without ever materializing an unbounded result. **Eligibility.** A provider's pairs are counted only when the provider is ELIGIBLE at build time: NOT sanctioned by the predicate below AND, when the deployment operates hardware trust, holding an active hardware-trust root (`expires_at` null or in the future) at `generated_at` — a registration that was never trusted is not supply evidence for a catalog admission, whatever it offered. **Sanction predicate (closed, current-state).** `provider_intake_sanctioned(provider_id, at)` — the ONE definition of "under an active route, trust, payout, or registration sanction" for SPEC-023 §16.2(b), which cites it by name — is true when ANY of the four categories holds at `at`, the snapshot build time, and a sanctioned provider is excluded from every key's count whatever it offered earlier: (1) **route sanction** — the provider's current SPEC-011 provisional-admission state is `rejected` (the admission manager's rejected set), OR the provider has a persisted SPEC-032 canary sanction with a non-zero fail count; both are the inputs the offer path consults today; (2) **trust sanction** — the deployment operates hardware trust and the provider holds NO active hardware-trust root at `at` (`hardware_verification_trust`, SPEC-014 §hardware trust): every root it ever held has been revoked or has expired, or it never held one; (3) **payout sanction** — no per-provider payout sanction state exists in the coordinator in v0.1.6 (SPEC-016 payout activation is a global operator switch, not a per-provider sanction), so this category is vacuous until a SPEC-016 amendment defines one, at which point it joins this predicate by amendment; (4) **registration sanction** — the provider has at least one revoked SPEC-002 provider token (SPEC-002 "Token rotation / revocation": `provider_tokens.revoked_at` set) and no active token, so its registration has been withdrawn rather than rotated. A route blacklist (`/admin/blacklist`) drains one live session and leaves no durable provider state; it is not a category here, and a blacklisted provider is sanctioned through (1) or (4) when the operator also rejects it or revokes its token. **Availability rule.** A sanction category the deployment does not operate (no hardware-trust store wired; provider tokens not required) contributes no sanction; a wired source that cannot be read at build time — a token issuer wired without its custody history included — makes the snapshot unavailable (no partial count is ever served). **Scope of the predicate.** It governs COUNTING only. The offer path keeps its v0.1.5 refusal set unchanged — a new offer is refused from a provider under a ROUTE sanction (category 1); a never-trusted or token-revoked provider may still submit an offer, which becomes supply evidence only once the provider is eligible at a later build — and a withdrawal is never gated on any category: a sanctioned provider can always withdraw. **Suppression.** A key whose distinct count is below `k_anonymity_min` is reported with `distinct_provider_offer_count: null` and `suppressed: true`, never as the small number. This key-attributable suppression is served ONLY to the operator credential class that already reads every per-provider offer through the listing, and it names no provider; the PUBLIC SPEC-023 §16.8 manifest never carries it — a suppressed row and an absent row are recorded there identically (`null`, `no_observations`, rule 4 [v0.10.4]). A key with no counted provider has no row. The response carries no provider id, candidate id, served model reference, pseudonym, hardware fingerprint, or per-provider field of any kind; the SPEC-023 §16.8 manifest records the SHA-256 of the exact response bytes as `distinct_provider_offer_source_sha256` and the operator retains the bytes in the private intake audit store (SPEC-023 §16.8 rule 9). **Errors**: `invalid_operator_token` (401), `invalid_request` (400), `rate_limited` (429), `intake_unavailable` (503).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:130:**[amended v0.1.5]** **Authority.** The coordinator's offer-time `catalog_match_state` is the ONE authority for a candidate's catalog identity; the SPEC-046-R003 `identity_state` value `catalog_matched` is CLI-local inventory (advisory; the v0.1.3 sentence above describes the coordinator's verification, which this paragraph specifies), and the provider-signed `catalog_model_key` of an offer or withdrawal is a provider claim never read as identity. **Match.** The coordinator performs the catalog match at OFFER time, on the signed `artifact_hashes` of the offer package, resolving every offered `(hash_algorithm, hash)` pair EXACTLY through the two independent paths SPEC-010-R007(b) defines: the **primary-row path** — a `(macprovider.snapshot-manifest.v1, model_sha256)` pair equal to the `model_sha256` of exactly one `listed`/`recommendable` candidate row of the CURRENT admitted release is a row-bound match that needs no artifact feed and carries no feed provenance (a pair equal to more than one row's digest is `primary_row_ambiguous` and matches nothing) — and the **feed path** — any other pair is resolved against the identity set of that release (its release-bound, fresh artifact feed's `verified` artifacts of `listed`/`recommendable` keys), and a release with no usable set (rate-card-bound, feed missing, stale, or integrity-failed) resolves nothing on this path while leaving the primary-row path untouched. A resolved member is admissible for the offer only when the offer's signed `runtime_source` is allowed for it: for an `artifact_feed` member, `runtime_source` ∈ the artifact's `allowed_runtime_sources` (SPEC-023 §3.7.4); for a `candidate_row` member — an `mlx_safetensors` artifact — the sources the SPEC-023 §3.7.4 matrix allows for that format (`mlx_cache`); a member whose sources exclude the offer's is inadmissible for this offer. **Match ordering is fixed:** (1) every offered pair is resolved raw through the two paths; (2) raw resolved pairs spanning two keys yield NO match (`artifact_hashes_span_keys`) before any admissibility filtering; (3) the runtime-source admissibility filter removes inadmissible members from the admissible member set — they are NOT recorded; (4) the offer is a catalog match when at least one admissible member remains (they all belong to one key by (2)); when (3) leaves none the offer is `unmatched` with `catalog_match_reason` = `runtime_source_not_allowed`. Because one offer carries one signed `runtime_source` and the SPEC-023 §3.7.4 matrix gives `mlx_safetensors` and `gguf` disjoint source sets, one offer records members of ONE runtime format: an `mlx_cache` offer records only the row-bound primary (and any other `mlx_safetensors` member), and a loopback offer records only the members its source allows. **Recorded on the offer event:** `catalog_match_state` ∈ {`catalog_matched`, `unmatched`}; `catalog_match_reason` ∈ {`none`, `no_artifact_match`, `catalog_model_key_disagrees`, `artifact_hashes_span_keys`, `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure`, `primary_row_ambiguous`, `runtime_source_not_allowed`}; for a match, `catalog_model_key` = the RESOLVED row key, the resolved row tuple read from the authenticated candidate catalog — `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256` — the release it was read from as PROVENANCE — `catalog_release_id`, `catalog_candidate_sha256` (the SPEC-023 candidate-catalog body digest; distinct from the SPEC-008 Tier-2 `catalog_body_digest` R003 binds), `catalog_signer_key_id` — and `catalog_members`, every resolved member as a tagged record: `source` ∈ {`candidate_row`, `artifact_feed`}, the pair, and for `artifact_feed` members `artifact_id` plus the provenance of the set it resolved in (`artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, `artifact_candidate_catalog_sha256`), all non-null; for a `candidate_row` member `artifact_id` and the three provenance fields are null (the candidate row defines no artifact id, SPEC-023 §3.2, and none is synthesized). There is no `primary` flag: the six-value obligation of SPEC-047-R003 / SPEC-010-R007(d) is keyed on `source` alone (every `artifact_feed` member carries the six values, the feed's primary entry included). A provider-offered `catalog_model_key` that is non-empty and differs from the resolved key yields NO match (`catalog_model_key_disagrees`); resolved pairs spanning two keys yield NO match (`artifact_hashes_span_keys`); a pair present under two keys or two artifact ids of one identity set is the SPEC-023 `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure` and yields NO match; no resolved pair is `no_artifact_match`. Unmatched offers stand as unmatched offers and MUST store `catalog_model_key` as null. **What a release re-stamp means.** The production catalog renewal re-stamps `version` (a date-embedded release id) and `generated_at` on a schedule while leaving rows and artifact sets untouched, and live sessions survive it as compatible-previous releases (SPEC-010-R004). Catalog identity is therefore anchored on CONTENT — the row tuple (`catalog_model_key`, `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256`) and, per member, `source`, `artifact_id`, and the pair — and the recorded release and feed provenance is evidence of the release the match was evaluated under, never an equality gate: a re-stamp that preserves the row tuple and the member set is a no-op for every recorded match and every admission, and the immutable route-time record (SPEC-047-R003) always carries the provenance of the release the SESSION is actually verified under, which is what settlement re-verifies. A recorded match is never recomputed for an old offer; a decision re-resolves the RECORDED content (R003), and a reload under which that content no longer resolves is drift (R006).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:156:**SPEC-047-R008 - Release evidence.** Promotion beyond draft MUST include automated tests for offer dry-run non-submission, provider signature verification, replay rejection, closed-schema unknown-field rejection, endpoint/origin/socket/path rejection including loopback, localhost, IPv6 loopback, encoded IP, redirect, Unix-socket, and local-path variants, state-machine transition validity including withdrawn/revoked re-offer freshness and, for rejection, that a synchronously rejected offer (HTTP 4xx, closed code) appends nothing and a fresh compliant offer is then accepted, `models admission status` presentation of provider-facing state meaning, next action, and earning-path disclosure, synthetic probes using the provider wire protocol rather than coordinator dereference, settlement-boundary enforcement, default buyer invisibility for non-settlement states, explicit experimental disclosure if implemented, pricing trust nullability, revocation on drift, withdrawal, sanction interaction, payload redaction, parser/resource bounds, and SPEC-044 economics gating. Localization and accessibility fixtures for `settlement_capable` MUST preserve **Eligible to earn on qualifying settled requests** as conditional eligibility and reject current-income, current-serving, guaranteed-demand, and guaranteed-settlement meanings. Fixtures for coordinator-backed `not_offered` MUST preserve the exact English source meaning **Coordinator reports no active network offer for this model.** and MUST distinguish it from SPEC-046 `local_default:not_offered`, which cannot assert offer history. Production promotion MUST include a signed journey result covering one rejected opaque endpoint, one sandbox-probe-only offer, one network-visible unpriced offer, one catalog-matched offer that is not yet settlement-capable, one novel non-catalog offer whose status says no earning path exists in v0.1, one synchronously rejected offer followed by a fresh accepted offer, one revoked drift case, one withdrawn re-entry requiring fresh evidence, and one settlement-capable catalog-verified case. **[amended v0.1.5]** Promotion MUST additionally include automated tests for: per-actor operator authentication (the shared `operator_key` is refused), the closed decision request/response grammars (unknown field, bad state, bad reason including every reserved internal reason and every withdrawal-enum value, bad idempotency key, malformed `expected_coordinator_event_id`), dual control on `settlement_capable` (same actor cannot approve; approval re-evaluates preconditions); precedence (`stale_head` before `invalid_transition` before precondition codes; identical replay answers the original event after the head advanced; divergent reuse fails; two concurrent first-seen requests with one key); a decision for a candidate with no offer; offer-time matching through both paths (row-bound primary with no usable set; feed-path member; an `mlx_cache` offer carrying a primary pair and a GGUF pair of one key records the primary member only, and the same pairs under a loopback source record the GGUF member only; raw pairs spanning keys rejected before admissibility filtering; a disagreeing asserted key; an integrity-failed set; an ambiguous primary row) with `catalog_match_reason` recorded and listed; the `listed` ceiling at decision time (`catalog_row_not_recommendable`); a release RE-STAMP (new release id, digest, and feed signature, unchanged rows and members) that changes NOTHING — no revocation, decisions still commit, sessions on the previous release still settle; a content change per field (key, `model_id`, `model_sha256` each independently, a member removed from the set, a feed dropped) that revokes with the matching code; the session-binding lifecycle (derive at hello and at offer; unmatched and ambiguous candidates bind nothing; refresh on decision; revocation refresh clears routability; clear on withdrawal/model change/disconnect; route-time event-id equality and bound-member content equality); `settlement_capable` with no bound verified session and with the single bound verified session, a replacing hello re-deriving the binding, and a session on a retained compatible-previous release verified in its own release's identity set; hello-time drift (initial hello after disconnect, replacement hello) lacking the receipt key or failing the pinned-member predicate revoking before the new session is observable as bound; decision-vs-revocation, decision-vs-reload (generation change fails the decision closed), decision-vs-hello/disconnect/model-change/offer-rebinding interleavings under the section; route-snapshot compare-and-insert against revocation, withdrawal, demotion, identity drift, row change, and reload (the attempt fails closed or the immutable snapshot stands); the reload sweeps over both `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable`; the offer-listing schema, ordering, cap, member bound, session facts, and provider isolation; operator rate limiting independent of the target provider's window; a value-semantics test that an unmatched offer yields `catalog_model_key: null` and `earning_path_class: no_earning_path_in_v0_1` while the `model_admission_status.v1` field set is unchanged; that every drift event records the actor and the reason, the reason readable through `models admission status` and the actor through the operator listing; `runtime_source_not_allowed` at match and decision time and `catalog_runtime_source_disallowed` on reload; the dual-control protocol (pending record; request replay answers the pending record; fewer than two configured actors → synchronous `dual_control_unavailable`, no record; approval by the same actor refused; approval after a head change refused and the record invalidated; expiry; identical-key approval retry answers the committed response; distinct-key double approval → one append + `pending_consumed`); a Tier-2 material change on reload revoking a surviving candidate (`catalog_row_changed`); a reader that observes the Tier-2 material, the catalog, and the identity sets of one and the same generation only (a staged reload is invisible until published); an approval whose path and body ids or bound fields disagree (`invalid_request`), a divergent approval body under a reused key (`invalid_request` under (a): every divergence of the closed body is a bound-field disagreement; the `idempotency_conflict` branch of (b) stays as defence in depth), and the pending-response values of the initial `settlement_capable` request; an offer appended for candidate B while a route attempt for candidate A of the same row is in flight — the attempt fails closed on the binding generation and an offer whose only resolvable member is disallowed for its `runtime_source` recorded as `unmatched` / `runtime_source_not_allowed` with an empty member set; a reader that starts a decision before a reload's write lock and one that starts after (the first appends under the old generation and is revalidated or revoked by the sweep before any route attempt succeeds; the second sees only the fully installed release); a route attempt between publication and the sweep reaching the candidate fails closed; and a second candidate for the same row appended while the first is routable — the binding generation makes the in-flight route attempt fail closed.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:158:**SPEC-047-R009 - Intake aggregate (v0.1.6).** The coordinator MUST serve `GET /admin/model-admission/intake` exactly as R001's **[amended v0.1.6] Intake aggregate** paragraph specifies: the closed `model_admission_intake_offer_counts.v1` frame with a per-build `nonce`; DISTINCT `(provider_id, intake_model_key)` pairs of the trailing 30 days anchored on the coordinator-assigned `created_at_utc`, the `intake_model_key` resolved at offer time against every candidate-catalog row and verified artifact; provider eligibility evaluated once per provider at build time (not sanctioned by `provider_intake_sanctioned`, and holding an active hardware-trust root where trust is operated); suppression below the fixed `k_anonymity_min` of 3 with no per-provider field; a 15-minute materialization under a 10-second timeout and a 100 000-pair ceiling; `intake_unavailable` (503) instead of any partial count; and the counting-only scope of the predicate (the offer gate keeps the v0.1.5 route-sanction refusal; withdrawal is never gated). Promotion beyond draft MUST include automated tests for: a provider counted once across several candidates; suppression of one- and two-provider keys; a never-trusted and an expired-trust provider excluded while trust is operated and counted while it is not; a rejected and a canary-sanctioned provider excluded; a revoked-token provider with no active token excluded and a rotated provider counted; an unreadable wired sanction source and a wired issuer without custody history leaving the previous snapshot in place; the pair ceiling; the inclusive second-granularity window on both stores; an `unmatched` offer for a `candidate` row counted toward that row's key; a withdrawn offer still counted; `intake_unavailable` before the first build and after two missed cadences; and the closed-frame rejection of an unknown key, a missing `nonce`, or a non-UTC timestamp by the SPEC-023 generator.
specs/SPEC-006-buyer-api.md:19:- Residual: if the buyer system prompt is unique per session (timestamps, session ids), the scaffold hash still misses across `--no-session` runs; ConversationCache LCP cannot skip a volatile prefix. Registers `SPEC-006-R014`.
specs/SPEC-006-buyer-api.md:300:- `SPEC-006-R014` — Auto-prefix tags hash the stable system+tools scaffold when
specs/SPEC-006-buyer-api.md:1783:- **(v0.9.28 auto-prefix algorithm — SPEC-006-R012, amended v0.9.31 / SPEC-006-R014:)** When no sticky key was derived for an authenticated non-demo chat completion request: (1) skip malformed `messages[]` objects that cannot be JSON-decoded to extract a role; (2) if no `role=="user"` message (case-insensitive) is found, do not derive a key; (3) collect the **scaffold** as every surviving message *before* the first user message, and take `tools` as the request `tools[]` JSON when it is a non-empty array (`null` and `[]` count as absent); (4) if the scaffold is non-empty **or** tools are present, `canonical_bytes = json.Marshal({"scaffold": scaffold, "tools": tools})` (omit `tools` when absent) — the first user message is **not** in this hash; (5) otherwise (user-only, no tools) `canonical_bytes = json.Marshal([]json.RawMessage(messages_through_first_user))` as in v0.9.28; (6) `prefix_hash = sha256(canonical_bytes)[:16]`; (7) `tag = "auto.prefix." + hex.EncodeToString(prefix_hash)`; (8) derive the `conv:` key with the § 1.3 HMAC using `account_id` and `tag`; (9) forward it as `X-MacProvider-Internal-Conv-Cache` (not `X-MacProvider-Internal-Conv`). Same scaffold across unique user questions ⇒ same tag ⇒ ConversationCache LCP can skip-prefill the shared prefix. Same first-user prefix across tool turns still shares a key. Different `account_id` ⇒ different key. This key MUST NOT activate SPEC-004 sticky affinity; coordinator `applySticky` / `stickyStore` MUST read only `X-MacProvider-Internal-Conv`.

specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:262:6. **Sole-provider floors apply to health/liveness uncertainty only — never to integrity violations, and never as a no-op.** This is the r3 correction to a genuinely dangerous r2 rule. A floor that spares the last provider from a *capacity, catalog-membership, hash, or admission* violation creates the attacker's ideal case: be the only provider for a model, then switch to an unadmitted model and remain buyer-serving as alert-only. Integrity violations **fail closed even if that empties the pool** — a 503 is the correct outcome when the alternative is knowingly routing buyers to an unadmitted model. FR-CAN22's floor (`pool/provider.go:1348`) stays scoped to canary/health uncertainty, where "we are unsure this provider is healthy" genuinely does not warrant destroying the only supply.
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:527:- **B2 — Ceiling enforcement** (was R3b). Turns A5's alert into action: over-ceiling/uncatalogued → routing-ineligible for that model; evidence-TTL added to the 30 s `trust_revalidation.go` sweep. **Its SPEC must resolve** the sole-provider case honestly (§5.3.6): integrity violations fail **closed** even when that empties the pool — the `CanaryTripFloorHeld` floor stays scoped to canary/health uncertainty, never to capacity/catalog/hash violations (the security lane's fail-open finding). Also: warm-up probe-target behavior when the ceiling changes (`providerProbeModelID` is the live consumer). Flips SPEC-032 AC-F1/AC-F2.

A manifest that names a suppressed signal as its `admission_clause`, that sets `coldstart_slot_used` on more entries than `INTAKE_COLDSTART_SLOTS`, or whose observation window ends more than one §16.5 cadence period before `as_of` fails closed. The manifest carries no provider id, pseudonym, hardware fingerprint, buyer account, API key, IP address, raw principal identifier, or §16.2(a) item-7 principal token in any field, hashed or otherwise. Given the manifest, its ledger-recorded digest, the release's signed feeds, and the retained intake audit store responses (rule 9), an auditor with access to the private intake audit store re-evaluates the §16.3 rule for every changed key and reaches the same verdict without re-running the generator. **[v0.10.4]** The test set MUST also cover rule 9 and the fixed floor: a recorded `*_source_sha256` that does not equal the retained file's digest fails closed; a retained source file the manifest does not cite fails closed; a missing audit store fails closed; a source whose `k_anonymity_min` is not 3, or a manifest `INTAKE_K_ANONYMITY_MIN` other than 3, fails closed; a manifest `thresholds` value that differs from the selected window's `parameters` fails closed; a source file with an unknown key fails closed; a recorded `distinct_provider_offer_count`, `fleet_fit_fraction_ppm`, or `unmatched_model_request_count` that the committed bytes do not reproduce fails closed; a non-null unmatched signal whose window is open, incomplete, or not the latest complete window fails closed; `unmatched_model_request_suppressed: true` fails closed against a `macprovider.stats-intake.v1` source; a null signal with a null digest whose reason is neither `spec017_amendment_not_landed` nor `source_unavailable` fails closed; and a manifest whose per-signal windows disagree with the committed sources, or whose `observation_window_*` envelope is not the min/max of them, fails closed. The test set MUST also cover: an `admit_listed` entry with a `null` `openrouter_demand_rank`, `distinct_provider_offer_count`, and `fleet_fit_fraction_ppm` each carrying its own non-null `*_absent_reason` (accepted); the same entry with a `null` signal and a `null` `*_absent_reason` (fails closed); a non-null signal with a non-null `*_absent_reason` (fails closed); and one `promote_recommendable` entry with `signals`, `admission_clause`, and `fit_clause` `null` and a complete `promotion` object (accepted) versus the same entry carrying an `admission_clause` value or a `null` `promotion` (fails closed).

specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:142:The successful closed response contains exactly: `version: relay-blind-reservation-v1`, `provider_binding`, `buyer_binding`, `key_record_digest`, `key_record`, `kid`, `endpoint_family`, `model`, `provider_model`, `stream`, `max_encrypted_request_bytes`, `max_output_tokens`, `input_token_upper_bound`, `reservation_token_cap`, `expires_at_unix`, `cache_policy: no-store`, and `failover_policy: disabled`. It contains no stable provider ID or assigned-session ID. Public success and error metadata MUST NOT expose `X-Provider-Id` or any equivalent stable peer identifier. TTL is at most 30 seconds and no later than signed key expiry.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:146:Before quota or dispatch, the gateway calls internal `POST /v1/relay-blind/consume` with the exact envelope and same trusted account/session context. The closed success response contains exactly `version: relay-blind-consume-v1`, `provider_binding`, `buyer_binding`, `envelope_digest`, `execution_authorization`, `consumed_at_unix`, and `expires_at_unix`. Consumption cannot dispatch. The authorization is opaque outside the coordinator and stored only as a hash in durable state. Buyer-supplied execution authorization is stripped; trusted authorization is carried only on the internal dispatch hop and stripped before any provider runtime/upstream request header set.
specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:148:Recovery uses authenticated internal `POST /v1/relay-blind/status` with exactly `provider_binding_digest` and `envelope_digest`, each canonical base64url SHA-256. The closed response contains `version: relay-blind-status-v1`, `state`, `internal_request_id`, `validated`, nullable `input_tokens`, nullable `completion_tokens`, `effective_privacy_outcome`, and `retry_action: do_not_resubmit`. Input is present exactly when authenticated usage is known; completion is present only for `terminal`. This endpoint never dispatches. It atomically fences expired `reserved` or `consumed_predispatch` rows to `rejected` before reporting them; fresh rows remain held to avoid a concurrent dispatch/refund race. `unknown_postdispatch` is irreversible and settles known input and locally recorded delivered output only. Usage knowledge and satisfied privacy are independent facts.

specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:272:The coordinator also exposes `POST /admin/trust-pools/pools/{pool_id}/signed-lifecycle` for R012 signed emergency restrictive lifecycle controls and R003 immediate revocation. The signed control message is domain-separated from policy-core and authority-log signatures, binds `pool_id`, the latest accepted `manifest_version` and `manifest_core_digest`, the authorizing signer set, an operation id, action, optional `target_provider_id`, reason, and a short validity window, and is honored only when signed either by the manifest authority root (`signer_set_version = 0`) or by the current operational signer set at threshold. A manifest update or authority-log rotation makes older control messages stale. `paused`, `draining`, and `retired` controls append the normal durable `lifecycle_changed` event with the signed-control body and signatures recorded in the event payload, then refresh the routeable registry fail-closed. `revoke_immediate` requires a non-empty `target_provider_id`, appends a proof-bearing durable `member_revoked` event for that provider, advances the same route-generation fence so new selection and stale selected dispatch fail closed, and cancels active uncommitted provider attempts by wrapping the shared dispatch request context in a revocation watcher. Already-committed streaming output remains terminal once bytes have been delivered to the buyer; `retired` controls now require delivery-drain proof, and `active` still requires promotion.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:284:**Authority-log entry encoding and chain verification.** Each authority-log entry has a canonically-encoded, domain-separated **content** (the hashed, chained part) plus the authorizing **signatures** (not hashed). The content grammar uses the same length-prefixed framing (SPEC-041-R002 precedent) under the fixed ASCII domain tag `macprovider/spec042/authority-log-entry/v1`, encoding in order: `pool_id` (binding the entry to its pool so it cannot be replayed into another pool's log — the log is keyed under `pool_id`), `signer_set_version` (`>= 1`; version 0 is reserved as the root-authorizer sentinel), `prev_authority_log_entry_hash` (32 bytes; genesis = 32 zero bytes), the signer key set (`key_id` + Ed25519 `public_key`, byte-lexicographically ordered by `key_id`, no duplicate id and no duplicate public key), the threshold `M`, the validity window (`not_before_unix`, `expires_at_unix`), the strictly-ascending, distinct `revokes_versions` list (rejected, not normalized, if out of order or duplicated), and `authorizing_signer_set_version` (0 = root issuer). `authority_log_entry_hash = SHA256(content)`; authorizers sign the domain-separated message `macprovider/spec042/authority-log-entry-sig/v1 ‖ authority_log_entry_hash` (a distinct signing tag so an authority-log signature can never be replayed as a policy-core signature). Replaying a log verifies, per entry: the established set is structurally valid (`1 ≤ M ≤ N`, distinct keys); `signer_set_version` strictly increases (rollback rejected); the prev-hash chain is intact; each `revokes_versions` entry is a prior existing version; and the entry is authorized either by exactly one root-issuer signature (`authorizing_signer_set_version = 0`) or by `M`-of-`N` of a prior, still-authorized (unrevoked, window-containing the entry's `not_before_unix`), lower-versioned signer set — with the authorization checked before the entry's own revocations apply, so a set may authorize its own replacement then be revoked. Replay binds the log to the pool identity (the supplied root-issuer key must match the identity core's `root_issuer_key_id`, and every entry's `pool_id` must equal the identity core's derived `pool_id`) and materializes `signer_set_version → SignerSet` (with revocation state, deep-copied so the verified signer material cannot be mutated through the caller's inputs) — the exact value policy-core verification consumes. This is implemented in `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/authoritylog.go` and frozen by golden vectors in `authoritylog_test.go`. The durable snapshot codec and verdict-replay **reconstruction** of the authority log + policy-core history + acceptance verdicts are implemented in slice 5 (`persist.go`, see the R011 reconstruction note); v0.0.15 locally wires accepted-manifest projection/high-water evidence into the coordinator store, while full authority-log snapshot persistence and highest-accepted signer-set rollback proof remain pending.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:315:- 0.0.20 - Added R012 signed emergency restrictive lifecycle controls. `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/control.go` defines the domain-separated emergency lifecycle control message and verifier: it binds `pool_id`, latest accepted manifest version/digest, signer-set version, operation id, action, reason, and validity window; accepts either manifest-authority-root signature (`signer_set_version = 0`) or threshold signatures from the current operational signer set; and rejects stale manifest/authority/time bindings. `POST /admin/trust-pools/pools/{pool_id}/signed-lifecycle` verifies the signed control against the reconstructed durable manifest snapshot before appending a `lifecycle_changed` event with persisted signed-control proof, then refreshes the routeable registry fail-closed. The endpoint deliberately supports only `paused`/`draining`/`retired`; `active` remains promotion-only and `revoke_immediate` remains a separate blocker requiring provider-specific revocation plus in-flight cutoff semantics. No requirement is promoted: signed journey evidence, production activation evidence, remaining predicate/status freshness blockers, `revoke_immediate`, and 0 C/H/M launch audit remain required.
specs/SPEC-042-pool-control-plane.md:325:- 0.0.10 - R012 implementation slice 3 (authority log): implemented the append-only, hash-chained **authority log** that establishes and versions the operational **signer sets** policy-core verification (slice 2) consumes. Defined the authority-log-entry content byte grammar (domain tag `macprovider/spec042/authority-log-entry/v1`) + `authority_log_entry_hash` + the distinct entry signing preimage, and the chain-replay verifier `BuildAuthorityLog(rootIssuer, entries)`: per-entry signer-set structural validation, strictly-monotonic `signer_set_version` (rollback rejected), prev-hash chain, `revokes_versions` (prior-existing only), and authorization by either one root-issuer signature or `M`-of-`N` of a prior still-authorized (unrevoked, window-containing) lower-versioned set — authorization evaluated before the entry's own revocations, enabling rotate-and-revoke. Replay materializes `signer_set_version → SignerSet` with revocation state. Extracted a shared `verifyThresholdMessage` primitive (policy-core verification byte-identical). Lives in `phase4-coordinator/internal/poolmanifest/authoritylog.go`, frozen by golden vectors (genesis → rotate → revoke). Binds each entry to its pool (`pool_id` in the content) and to the identity core's root issuer so a log signed under a reused root key cannot be replayed into another pool; reserves `signer_set_version = 0`; rejects non-ascending `revokes_versions`; and deep-copies materialized signer material. Closes the last deferred R001/R012 canonical-encoding deliverable. Pure (no I/O/persistence/wall-clock); durable persistence + restart reconstruction + the acceptance-verdict record remain a later slice. Default-inert.
