specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:141:**SPEC-045-R005 - Restart-safe budget ledger.** When a cumulative run budget is configured, the command MUST persist a local exposure ledger under the default user-private state path `$HOME/Library/Application Support/macprovider/consume/ledgers/default.jsonl` on macOS unless the operator supplies an explicit ledger path, and it MUST hold an OS-enforced exclusive advisory file lock on a lock file named `<ledger-filename>.lock` adjacent to the ledger. The lock MUST use OS lock state, not lockfile presence; a stale lock file from a crashed process MUST NOT prevent a new process from acquiring the lock after the OS releases the prior lock on process termination. Ledger path class values MUST be the closed enum `default_user_state`, `explicit_absolute`, or `explicit_relative`; explicit relative ledger paths MUST resolve relative to the current working directory captured at process startup. The implementation MUST refuse any mode that creates a ledger, including budgeted mode and `--no-budget --ledger <path>`, when the state path is not user-private, is symlink-ambiguous, is not on a local filesystem with verified exclusive-lock semantics, or cannot be locked by exactly one active process. Implementations MUST verify local filesystem lock support using OS metadata such as `statfs`/`fstatfs` or a stronger platform-specific check, and MUST fail closed when the filesystem type or mount properties cannot be verified as local with real exclusive-lock semantics. A state path is symlink-ambiguous when the ledger path, lock path, or any parent directory resolves through a symlink that is not owned by the current OS user, or when the resolved target changes between validation and open/lock. Passing `--ledger <path>` without either `--budget-usd <amount>` or `--no-budget` MUST fail startup with `local_budget_flag_rejected` rather than creating an idle ledger whose admission mode is ambiguous. When `--no-budget` is combined with an explicit `--ledger <path>`, the ledger MUST be created, locked, and written with per-request no-budget records; the ledger path class is `explicit_absolute` or `explicit_relative` as appropriate. When `--no-budget` is used without an explicit `--ledger`, no ledger is created and per-request no-budget state is in-memory only. The ledger MUST record schema version `local_consumer_endpoint.ledger.v1`, immutable process launch id (`run_id`), a unique local `reservation_id` generated from at least 128 bits of CSPRNG input for every reservation, the same `run_id` and `reservation_id` copied onto every later state transition and audit row for that reservation, redacted request ids, model id, admission estimate or JSON null when `--no-budget` skips admission estimation, unpriced-override flag, no-budget flag when applicable, terminal local outcome, settled exposure amount when known, upstream request id when available, reservation state (`reserved`, `settled`, `held`, `released`, or `estimate_exceeded`), and created/updated timestamps; it MUST NOT record raw prompts, raw completions, bearer tokens, local bearer tokens, raw receipts, full upstream error bodies, hostnames, OS usernames, hardware serials, MAC addresses, or stable hardware UUIDs. A budgeted admission reservation MUST NOT be considered committed and MUST NOT be forwarded upstream until the ledger reservation append is durable; durable means the append bytes and required file metadata have been flushed with `fsync()` or a platform-equivalent durability primitive on the ledger file descriptor, and any newly created parent directory entry has been flushed with a platform-equivalent directory sync where supported. Every ledger state-transition append, including settlement, `estimate_exceeded`, held, released, and recovery audit entries, MUST satisfy the same durability rule before any local HTTP response, status output, recovery-command output, remaining-budget value, or restart-recovery decision relies on that transition. If a durable append fails, including fsync failure, the implementation MUST roll back any affected in-process reservation state when possible, mark ledger health unhealthy, return `local_budget_ledger_unavailable` for runtime chargeable paths, fail recovery commands nonzero without claiming success, and stop accepting chargeable requests until ledger health is restored. After a terminal upstream response, the ledger MUST settle a reservation to trusted upstream usage/cost evidence when such evidence is available, even when that evidence exceeds the admission estimate; if trusted usage/cost evidence is unavailable, it MUST settle to the admission estimate rather than inventing a lower cost. If trusted upstream usage/cost evidence exceeds the admission estimate, the ledger MUST record state `estimate_exceeded`, remaining budget MUST be allowed to reach zero or a negative value, status MUST surface the pricing-invariant breach, and the process MUST stop accepting new chargeable admission requests until restarted with corrected trusted pricing metadata or an explicit operator recovery path defined by a later spec; in-flight requests that already passed admission before `estimate_exceeded` was set MUST be allowed to complete. SPEC-005 billing and settlement remain authoritative. If the local client disconnects during streaming before trusted terminal usage/cost evidence is available, the implementation MUST cancel or close the upstream request when possible, wait no longer than one second for synchronous cancellation acknowledgement, and settle the reservation to the admission estimate unless the upstream returns trusted partial usage/cost evidence bound to the request. In-flight reservations MUST be treated conservatively on process restart: they become `held` and reduce remaining budget until a recovery command updates them. On graceful shutdown, including SIGTERM, the process MUST stop accepting new requests, drain in-flight requests for a bounded period no longer than five seconds, settle terminal requests, cancel or close remaining upstream requests, mark remaining in-flight reservations `held`, remove the active endpoint descriptor when possible, and then exit. Operators should expect long-running streaming requests that exceed the five-second drain bound to become held reservations requiring recovery-command handling; that operational cost is intentional in v0.1 because bounded shutdown takes precedence over waiting indefinitely. R005 conformance REQUIRES local recovery commands named `malibu-cli consume budget status` and `malibu-cli consume budget release-held`; `status` MUST show redacted held reservations, age, estimate, and ledger path class, while `release-held` MUST require a ledger selector `--ledger <path>` or `--ledger default`, a run selector `--run-id <process-launch-id>`, and `--confirm-release-held`, MUST fail rather than modify the ledger while another process holds the ledger lock, MUST only release held local reservations whose immutable `run_id` exactly matches that selected run, MUST append a redacted audit entry carrying the same `run_id` and each released `reservation_id`, MUST leave wrong-run and missing-reservation rows unchanged, and MUST NOT alter settled local exposure or upstream gateway records. `--ledger default` on recovery commands MUST resolve to the macOS default path computed at recovery-command invocation time from the invoking user's `$HOME`. Manual ledger deletion is not a conformant recovery path. If the ledger cannot be opened, locked, parsed, or written, budgeted mode MUST refuse to start or MUST stop accepting chargeable requests.
specs/SPEC-040-wallet-native-buyer-sessions.md:197:`raw_body_sha256` is computed over the pre-translation HTTP request body bytes. Signed metadata routes (`GET /v1/models`, self status, self usage, and self revoke) MUST reject non-empty request bodies; their body hash is SHA-256 of the empty byte string. Query strings are forbidden on `mps_` self-service and `/v1/models` routes in v0.1; signed self-usage is summary-only. Paginated account-key list/usage may use query parameters because those routes are not session-authenticated. `X-MacProvider-Session-Timestamp` MUST equal `timestamp_unix` in the signed object. Default freshness is max age 300 seconds and max future skew 30 seconds, configurable only to a stricter value in production. Requests outside the freshness window fail with `wallet_session_signature_stale`. Replay records MUST be retained for at least the active session lifetime plus the settlement recovery window; if a deployment cannot prove retention for a session, it MUST reject that session's signed requests rather than prune replay rows early.
specs/SPEC-040-wallet-native-buyer-sessions.md:309:Schema-only additive migrations MAY run while wallet sessions are disabled, but this SPEC does not require old binaries to open a database after the new binary stamps an unknown `schema_migrations` version. The accepted rollback posture is fail-closed old-binary startup plus operator restore from the pre-deploy database snapshot only before any post-snapshot buyer/auth/money-path traffic is served. If post-snapshot traffic has occurred, rollback requires maintenance/drain plus preservation and reconciliation of every post-snapshot gateway effect before the old binary may serve traffic. Disabled runtime mode MUST mount no wallet-session creation/list/status/usage/revoke routes. Existing shared routes that are still mounted, such as inference and `/v1/models`, MUST return `wallet_sessions_disabled` when presented with an `mps_` credential while the feature is disabled; unmounted wallet-session extension endpoints MAY return the gateway's normal SPEC-006 404. Disabled mode MUST NOT require wallet-session secrets and MUST leave API-key, demo, quota, settlement, and existing auth behavior unchanged. Local implementation evidence MUST cover fresh disabled startup, enable-after-upgrade, disable-after-use, and idempotent migration reruns. Release acceptance evidence MUST additionally cover fail-closed old-binary rollback against a post-migration DB, successful old-binary startup after snapshot restore with zero post-snapshot rows, and the drain/reconciliation gate when post-snapshot traffic exists.

specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:107:**[amended v0.1.5]** The authorized actor `coordinator admission policy` acts, for OPERATOR-origin decisions to `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `settlement_capable`, and `revoked`, through exactly one production caller: an **operator decision request** `POST /admin/model-admission/decisions`. **Credential and attribution.** The request is authenticated with the per-actor coordinator operator credential class (`auth.operator_keys`, the class the `/admin` trust-granting surfaces use, which yields an operator actor id) — never the shared single-value `operator_key` — and the appended event's `actor` is `operator:<actor id>` (grammar `^operator:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`). The `settlement_capable` edge, the money-path grant, is **dual-control** exactly as `/admin/hardware-trust/approve` is: the request appends NO event: after steps (1)–(4) below succeed it durably records a pending decision (`pending_decision_id`, grammar `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`; the request's canonical body digest; the evaluated head; `requested_by`; `created_at`; a 24-hour expiry) and answers `model_admission_decision.v1` with the pending values: `previous_admission_state` and `admission_state` both the unchanged current state, `reason_code` the request's reason, `coordinator_event_id` the evaluated head, `accepted_at` the pending record's creation time, `decided_by` the requesting actor, `replayed` false, `pending_decision_id` set, `bound_member` null; a replay of that request answers the same pending record (`replayed: true`); a pending record is consumed by exactly one approval, expires unused, and is invalidated by any event appended for the candidate. `POST /admin/model-admission/decisions/<pending_decision_id>/approve` with request schema `model_admission_decision_approve_request.v1` (exactly `schema`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `pending_decision_id`, `expected_coordinator_event_id`, `idempotency_key`; same grammars) by a DISTINCT operator actor (the same actor is `dual_control_required`; when fewer than two distinct operator actors are configured, the initial `settlement_capable` request itself is refused synchronously with `dual_control_unavailable` and no pending record is created) commits the append under this approval precedence, executed as one unit inside the provider's section: (a) the path and body `pending_decision_id` MUST be equal and the body's `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, and `expected_coordinator_event_id` MUST equal the pending record's stored values, else `invalid_request`; (b) approval idempotency — the approval body is canonicalized and digested under (`pending_decision_id`, `idempotency_key`): an identical digest answers the committed response (`replayed: true`), a different digest under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`, both before any pending or head check — and because the closed approval body carries nothing but the bound fields and the key, every divergent body under a reused key is a bound-field disagreement already answered by (a), so (a) precedes (b) and `idempotency_conflict` on an approval is defence in depth; (c) pending status — consumed `pending_consumed`, expired `pending_expired`, invalidated or unknown `no_pending_decision`; (d) distinct actor, else `dual_control_required`; (e) the candidate's current head MUST still equal the pending record's evaluated head, else `stale_head` and the record is invalidated; (f) the SPEC-047-R003 preconditions re-evaluated in full; (g) release-generation re-compare and append; an unknown or invalidated id is `no_pending_decision`, an expired one `pending_expired`, a consumed one `pending_consumed`; approvals replay in their own namespace (`pending_decision_id`, `idempotency_key`): an identical-key retry of a committed approval answers the original committed response with `replayed: true`, whatever happened since; a distinct-key approval of a consumed record is `pending_consumed`; two concurrent distinct-key approvals resolve, under the section, as one append and one `pending_consumed`. The other four edges commit on the request. **Bounds.** The request is bounded by payload size and parser work like every SPEC-047-R007 mutation and rate-limited per operator credential and source address; it MUST NOT draw on any per-provider rate window, so a provider cannot exhaust an operator's ability to append a decision for its own candidates. **Request schema** `model_admission_decision_request.v1`, fields exactly `schema`, `provider_id` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`), `candidate_id` (`^byom_[a-z2-7]{52}$`), `next_state` (one of the five), `reason_code` (`^operator_[a-z0-9_]{2,56}$` — the `operator_` prefix is the operator origin's reserved namespace), `expected_coordinator_event_id` (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`), and `idempotency_key` (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`); unknown fields are rejected before any state transition. **Precedence**, executed as one unit inside the provider's decision critical section (below): (1) idempotency — the request is canonicalized and keyed by (`provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `idempotency_key`) (the store's replay index is extended to that triple); an identical canonical request answers with the result it originally produced — the appended event, or the pending decision — whatever the current head, marked `replayed: true`; the same key with a different body fails closed (`idempotency_conflict`); two concurrent first-seen requests with one key resolve as one append plus one replay or one append plus one conflict, never `stale_head`; (2) head compare — `expected_coordinator_event_id` must equal the candidate's current head, else `stale_head`; (3) edge validation against this table from the latest state, else `invalid_transition`; (4) for `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable` only, the SPEC-047-R003 preconditions in their stated order, each with its own code (the other three edges skip this step); (5) under the release read lock (below), the release-generation re-compare and the append as one unit; the appended event records `evaluated_release_generation`. The first failure wins and nothing is appended. **Head and event ids.** `coordinator_event_id` is unique per (`provider_id`, `candidate_id`) — the store's `UNIQUE(provider_id, request_id)` plus the event's own content digest — and the head is the event with the highest append sequence for that candidate, never a content comparison. **Response schema** `model_admission_decision.v1`, exactly `schema`, `generated_at`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `previous_admission_state`, `admission_state`, `reason_code`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, `decided_by` (the actor id), `replayed`, nullable `pending_decision_id`, and — non-null exactly for a committed `settlement_capable` — `bound_member` (`source`, nullable `artifact_id`, `hash_algorithm`, `hash`). `model_admission_status.v1` (SPEC-047-R002) keeps its exact field set; its value semantics change in one place, stated in R002. **Transition origins and reason sets are closed and disjoint:** the operator origin appends only the five edges above with `operator_`-prefixed reasons; the offer path appends `offer_submitted` with `provider_offer_submitted`; the withdrawal path appends `withdrawn` with the SPEC-047-R002 withdrawal enum; the synthetic-probe path appends `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, or `revoked` with `synthetic_probe_`-prefixed reasons; the drift path appends `revoked` with exactly one of `runtime_identity_drift`, `catalog_artifact_feed_changed`, `catalog_row_changed`, `catalog_row_ineligible`, `catalog_runtime_source_disallowed`, `receipt_key_unavailable`. Each origin emits only its own REASON set (three target states have two origins); a reason from another origin's set is `invalid_request`. `offer_rejected` is unreachable in v0.1.5: offer validation rejects synchronously (HTTP 4xx, closed code, nothing appended) and no origin appends that edge; the table row stays for a later validator lane, and the R008 rejected-offer cases are stated in terms of synchronous rejection. **Decision critical section.** It is scoped per `provider_id`: every decision and approval, drift event, session-to-candidate binding derivation or mutation (SPEC-047-R003 — whose uniqueness predicate spans all of a provider's candidates), and reload-sweep step for any of the provider's candidates takes that provider's section, and a section is never taken while the provider-registry lock is held (lock order: section, then registry). The provider's section also owns a monotonic **binding generation**, incremented under the section, in the same critical region as the append itself, on every event appended for any of the provider's candidates and on every binding mutation. **Release lock and generation.** The coordinator holds one release read-write lock over ONE immutable release snapshot — the candidate catalog, the compatible-previous catalogs, the artifact feeds and every per-release identity set, the Tier-2 catalog material, and the generation. A reload stages all of them and then takes the WRITE side to swap the whole snapshot and publish its monotonic generation as one act; no part of a release is ever visible before the others. Decisions and approvals take the READ side across the WHOLE evaluation — steps (1)–(5), including every R003 read of catalog rows, identity sets, runtime-source policy, and Tier-2 material — offer-time matching takes it across the match, session identity verification takes it across the verdict, and route-time snapshot creation takes it across the compare-and-insert. **Every append origin takes the provider section**: the offer path, the offer validator, the withdrawal path, the synthetic-probe path, the operator path, and the drift path each acquire the provider's section BEFORE reading candidate state and hold it through the event append, the invalidation of pending decisions for that candidate, the binding-generation increment, and the binding refresh or clear — one linearization point, so no route attempt can observe a candidate set the append has already changed. After publication the R006 sweeps take each provider's section in turn and stamp every surviving `catalog_priced`/`settlement_capable` candidate's binding with `validated_release_generation` = the new generation (a candidate the sweep has not yet reached is unroutable, not revoked). BYOM route-time snapshot creation (SPEC-047-R003) takes no provider section: under the release read lock it is an atomic compare-and-insert that re-reads, immediately before the insert, the candidate's head, the session binding and its `bound_coordinator_event_id`, the provider's binding generation captured at evaluation, and requires the binding's `validated_release_generation` to equal the published release generation; any difference fails the attempt closed. **Offer listing.** An operator decides on recorded state, never on a provider's claim: `GET /admin/model-admission/offers?provider_id=<id>` (same credential class; `provider_id` validated by its grammar, any other query parameter rejected) answers `model_admission_offer_list.v1`, exactly `schema`, `generated_at`, `provider_id`, `candidates` — ordered by `candidate_id`, bounded by the per-provider candidate cap — each item exactly `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, `runtime_source` (persisted on the offer event from v0.1.5), `admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `state_observed_at`, `reason_code`, `catalog_match_state`, `catalog_match_reason`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, nullable `catalog_row_model_id`, nullable `catalog_row_model_sha256`, nullable `catalog_release_id`, nullable `catalog_candidate_sha256`, nullable `catalog_signer_key_id`, `catalog_members` (at most 16 tagged members, each exactly `source`, `hash_algorithm`, `hash`, and nullable `artifact_id`, `artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, `artifact_candidate_catalog_sha256` — null exactly when `source` is `candidate_row`), `last_event_actor`, and `session` (nullable: `bound`, `bound_coordinator_event_id`, `validated_release_generation`, `verified_member` as a member record or null, `receipt_key_present`, `catalog_release_id`) — the live-session facts R003(iv) will evaluate; the actor of every event (drift included) is readable here, while `model_admission_status.v1` exposes the reason only. A decision request for a candidate with no offer fails closed (`no_offer`). **Errors** on all three endpoints use the existing `{"error":{"code","message"}}` envelope with exactly: `invalid_operator_token` (401), `invalid_request` (400), `no_offer` (404), `stale_head`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_transition`, `catalog_match_required`, `catalog_match_stale`, `catalog_row_not_recommendable`, `catalog_material_unavailable`, `no_verified_session`, `dual_control_required`, `dual_control_unavailable`, `no_pending_decision`, `pending_expired`, `pending_consumed`, `runtime_source_not_allowed` (all 409), and `rate_limited` (429).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:126:`schema` is that literal; `nonce` is 32 lowercase hex characters drawn from a cryptographically secure source at every build, so the SHA-256 the SPEC-023 §16.8 manifest records identifies ONE build even when two builds carry identical rows and the same second (the retained file is one read of one build, never a byte-equal replay of an earlier one); `generated_at`, `window_start`, and `window_end` are RFC3339 UTC timestamps with second precision in the one form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, `window_end == generated_at` and `window_start == generated_at − 30 days` exactly; `k_anonymity_min` is the integer `3` — SPEC-023 v0.10.4 §16.4 fixes `INTAKE_K_ANONYMITY_MIN` at 3 for that revision, and a different floor requires a lockstep amendment of SPEC-023, SPEC-017, and this SPEC; `rows` is an array ordered by `catalog_model_key` ascending (UTF-8 bytes) with no repeated key, each element exactly `catalog_model_key` (a SPEC-023 §3.2 normalized catalog key, `[a-z0-9._/-]{1,128}`), `distinct_provider_offer_count` (an integer ≥ `k_anonymity_min`, or `null`), and `suppressed` (a boolean; `true` exactly when the count is `null`). **Materialized snapshot, not a per-request scan.** The coordinator builds the aggregate on a fixed cadence — every 15 minutes, and once at startup — as one bounded job: one indexed scan of `offer_submitted` events with coordinator `created_at_utc` in the window (the store's admission-event table indexes `(state, created_at_utc)`), under a query timeout of 10 seconds and a hard ceiling of 100 000 DISTINCT `(provider_id, intake_model_key)` pairs; a job that exceeds either, or that cannot read every sanction source below, produces NO snapshot and leaves the previous one in place. **Consistency.** The build reads the offer events first, as one scan, and then evaluates the sanction predicate once per counted provider; the snapshot therefore reflects offers as of `generated_at` and sanctions as of a moment at or after it, which is monotone in the safe direction — a sanction applied during the build is honoured, a sanction lifted during it shows at the next build — and no partial snapshot is ever published (the snapshot pointer is swapped once, after every provider is evaluated). `GET` reads the current snapshot only (constant work per request; it is still rate-limited per operator credential and source address like the other operator endpoints and appends nothing) and answers `intake_unavailable` (503) when no snapshot exists, the newest is older than two cadences (30 minutes), or the newest is dated in the future (a clock step never serves a snapshot as current); `generated_at` is the snapshot's build time. **Window anchor.** Membership is decided by the event's coordinator-assigned append time — the admission-event row's `created_at_utc` column, set by the coordinator when it appends the event — never by any provider-signed timestamp in the offer package. **Counting rule.** A provider counts once for catalog key `K` when at least one `offer_submitted` event appended for that provider by the offer path with `created_at_utc` in `[window_start, window_end]` carries `intake_model_key == K`. `intake_model_key` is recorded on the offer event AT OFFER TIME by a resolution that is DISTINCT from the v0.1.5 `catalog_match_state`: the signed `artifact_hashes` of the offer are resolved against EVERY row of the current admitted release's candidate catalog by primary digest (`candidate`, `watch`, `listed`, and `recommendable` rows alike — the point of the signal is supply for keys the catalog has NOT admitted, which the v0.1.5 match, restricted to `listed`/`recommendable` rows, can never name) and against the release's usable identity set of verified artifacts; a pair that resolves to more than one row, or pairs that span two keys, resolve to no key. The provider-asserted `catalog_model_key` and `served_model_ref` are never read. An offer whose hashes resolve to no key carries an empty `intake_model_key` and counts for none. The offer's `catalog_match_state` is irrelevant to counting: a `catalog_matched` offer for a listed key counts toward that key (existing supply is still supply), and an `unmatched` offer for a `candidate` row counts toward that row's key. Later withdrawal, revocation, or drift does not un-count an offer (the signal is recorded interest, not current state); a provider offering `K` from several candidates counts once. The scan is over DISTINCT `(provider_id, intake_model_key)` pairs of the window — bounded by providers × keys, never by event volume — and the ceiling below applies to pairs and is enforced AT THE STORE: the store reads at most ceiling + 1 pairs (a SQL `LIMIT`; the in-memory store stops appending), so the build fails closed on the ceiling without ever materializing an unbounded result. **Eligibility.** A provider's pairs are counted only when the provider is ELIGIBLE at build time: NOT sanctioned by the predicate below AND, when the deployment operates hardware trust, holding an active hardware-trust root (`expires_at` null or in the future) at `generated_at` — a registration that was never trusted is not supply evidence for a catalog admission, whatever it offered. **Sanction predicate (closed, current-state).** `provider_intake_sanctioned(provider_id, at)` — the ONE definition of "under an active route, trust, payout, or registration sanction" for SPEC-023 §16.2(b), which cites it by name — is true when ANY of the four categories holds at `at`, the snapshot build time, and a sanctioned provider is excluded from every key's count whatever it offered earlier: (1) **route sanction** — the provider's current SPEC-011 provisional-admission state is `rejected` (the admission manager's rejected set), OR the provider has a persisted SPEC-032 canary sanction with a non-zero fail count; both are the inputs the offer path consults today; (2) **trust sanction** — the deployment operates hardware trust and the provider holds NO active hardware-trust root at `at` (`hardware_verification_trust`, SPEC-014 §hardware trust): every root it ever held has been revoked or has expired, or it never held one; (3) **payout sanction** — no per-provider payout sanction state exists in the coordinator in v0.1.6 (SPEC-016 payout activation is a global operator switch, not a per-provider sanction), so this category is vacuous until a SPEC-016 amendment defines one, at which point it joins this predicate by amendment; (4) **registration sanction** — the provider has at least one revoked SPEC-002 provider token (SPEC-002 "Token rotation / revocation": `provider_tokens.revoked_at` set) and no active token, so its registration has been withdrawn rather than rotated. A route blacklist (`/admin/blacklist`) drains one live session and leaves no durable provider state; it is not a category here, and a blacklisted provider is sanctioned through (1) or (4) when the operator also rejects it or revokes its token. **Availability rule.** A sanction category the deployment does not operate (no hardware-trust store wired; provider tokens not required) contributes no sanction; a wired source that cannot be read at build time — a token issuer wired without its custody history included — makes the snapshot unavailable (no partial count is ever served). **Scope of the predicate.** It governs COUNTING only. The offer path keeps its v0.1.5 refusal set unchanged — a new offer is refused from a provider under a ROUTE sanction (category 1); a never-trusted or token-revoked provider may still submit an offer, which becomes supply evidence only once the provider is eligible at a later build — and a withdrawal is never gated on any category: a sanctioned provider can always withdraw. **Suppression.** A key whose distinct count is below `k_anonymity_min` is reported with `distinct_provider_offer_count: null` and `suppressed: true`, never as the small number. This key-attributable suppression is served ONLY to the operator credential class that already reads every per-provider offer through the listing, and it names no provider; the PUBLIC SPEC-023 §16.8 manifest never carries it — a suppressed row and an absent row are recorded there identically (`null`, `no_observations`, rule 4 [v0.10.4]). A key with no counted provider has no row. The response carries no provider id, candidate id, served model reference, pseudonym, hardware fingerprint, or per-provider field of any kind; the SPEC-023 §16.8 manifest records the SHA-256 of the exact response bytes as `distinct_provider_offer_source_sha256` and the operator retains the bytes in the private intake audit store (SPEC-023 §16.8 rule 9). **Errors**: `invalid_operator_token` (401), `invalid_request` (400), `rate_limited` (429), `intake_unavailable` (503).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:130:**[amended v0.1.5]** **Authority.** The coordinator's offer-time `catalog_match_state` is the ONE authority for a candidate's catalog identity; the SPEC-046-R003 `identity_state` value `catalog_matched` is CLI-local inventory (advisory; the v0.1.3 sentence above describes the coordinator's verification, which this paragraph specifies), and the provider-signed `catalog_model_key` of an offer or withdrawal is a provider claim never read as identity. **Match.** The coordinator performs the catalog match at OFFER time, on the signed `artifact_hashes` of the offer package, resolving every offered `(hash_algorithm, hash)` pair EXACTLY through the two independent paths SPEC-010-R007(b) defines: the **primary-row path** — a `(macprovider.snapshot-manifest.v1, model_sha256)` pair equal to the `model_sha256` of exactly one `listed`/`recommendable` candidate row of the CURRENT admitted release is a row-bound match that needs no artifact feed and carries no feed provenance (a pair equal to more than one row's digest is `primary_row_ambiguous` and matches nothing) — and the **feed path** — any other pair is resolved against the identity set of that release (its release-bound, fresh artifact feed's `verified` artifacts of `listed`/`recommendable` keys), and a release with no usable set (rate-card-bound, feed missing, stale, or integrity-failed) resolves nothing on this path while leaving the primary-row path untouched. A resolved member is admissible for the offer only when the offer's signed `runtime_source` is allowed for it: for an `artifact_feed` member, `runtime_source` ∈ the artifact's `allowed_runtime_sources` (SPEC-023 §3.7.4); for a `candidate_row` member — an `mlx_safetensors` artifact — the sources the SPEC-023 §3.7.4 matrix allows for that format (`mlx_cache`); a member whose sources exclude the offer's is inadmissible for this offer. **Match ordering is fixed:** (1) every offered pair is resolved raw through the two paths; (2) raw resolved pairs spanning two keys yield NO match (`artifact_hashes_span_keys`) before any admissibility filtering; (3) the runtime-source admissibility filter removes inadmissible members from the admissible member set — they are NOT recorded; (4) the offer is a catalog match when at least one admissible member remains (they all belong to one key by (2)); when (3) leaves none the offer is `unmatched` with `catalog_match_reason` = `runtime_source_not_allowed`. Because one offer carries one signed `runtime_source` and the SPEC-023 §3.7.4 matrix gives `mlx_safetensors` and `gguf` disjoint source sets, one offer records members of ONE runtime format: an `mlx_cache` offer records only the row-bound primary (and any other `mlx_safetensors` member), and a loopback offer records only the members its source allows. **Recorded on the offer event:** `catalog_match_state` ∈ {`catalog_matched`, `unmatched`}; `catalog_match_reason` ∈ {`none`, `no_artifact_match`, `catalog_model_key_disagrees`, `artifact_hashes_span_keys`, `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure`, `primary_row_ambiguous`, `runtime_source_not_allowed`}; for a match, `catalog_model_key` = the RESOLVED row key, the resolved row tuple read from the authenticated candidate catalog — `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256` — the release it was read from as PROVENANCE — `catalog_release_id`, `catalog_candidate_sha256` (the SPEC-023 candidate-catalog body digest; distinct from the SPEC-008 Tier-2 `catalog_body_digest` R003 binds), `catalog_signer_key_id` — and `catalog_members`, every resolved member as a tagged record: `source` ∈ {`candidate_row`, `artifact_feed`}, the pair, and for `artifact_feed` members `artifact_id` plus the provenance of the set it resolved in (`artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, `artifact_candidate_catalog_sha256`), all non-null; for a `candidate_row` member `artifact_id` and the three provenance fields are null (the candidate row defines no artifact id, SPEC-023 §3.2, and none is synthesized). There is no `primary` flag: the six-value obligation of SPEC-047-R003 / SPEC-010-R007(d) is keyed on `source` alone (every `artifact_feed` member carries the six values, the feed's primary entry included). A provider-offered `catalog_model_key` that is non-empty and differs from the resolved key yields NO match (`catalog_model_key_disagrees`); resolved pairs spanning two keys yield NO match (`artifact_hashes_span_keys`); a pair present under two keys or two artifact ids of one identity set is the SPEC-023 `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure` and yields NO match; no resolved pair is `no_artifact_match`. Unmatched offers stand as unmatched offers and MUST store `catalog_model_key` as null. **What a release re-stamp means.** The production catalog renewal re-stamps `version` (a date-embedded release id) and `generated_at` on a schedule while leaving rows and artifact sets untouched, and live sessions survive it as compatible-previous releases (SPEC-010-R004). Catalog identity is therefore anchored on CONTENT — the row tuple (`catalog_model_key`, `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256`) and, per member, `source`, `artifact_id`, and the pair — and the recorded release and feed provenance is evidence of the release the match was evaluated under, never an equality gate: a re-stamp that preserves the row tuple and the member set is a no-op for every recorded match and every admission, and the immutable route-time record (SPEC-047-R003) always carries the provenance of the release the SESSION is actually verified under, which is what settlement re-verifies. A recorded match is never recomputed for an old offer; a decision re-resolves the RECORDED content (R003), and a reload under which that content no longer resolves is drift (R006).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:134:**SPEC-047-R002 - Offer package schema.** `malibu-cli models offer <candidate> --dry-run --json` MUST produce a local preflight result and MUST NOT submit state. `malibu-cli models offer <candidate> --json` MUST submit a provider-signed offer package only after the operator confirms the candidate, runtime source, served model reference, disclosure class, and non-earning states. The recommended provider workflow is `models discover --json`, `models evaluate <candidate> --json`, `models offer <candidate> --dry-run --json`, and then `models offer <candidate> --json`. Offer dry-run output MUST use a closed JSON envelope with `schema: "model_admission_offer_dry_run.v1"` and MUST include `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `would_submit`, `likely_admission_state`, `likely_admission_state_source`, `provider_guidance`, nullable `reason_code`, and `warnings`; `likely_admission_state_source` MUST be `local_default` or `coordinator`; when it is `local_default`, `likely_admission_state` MUST be `local_only`, `not_offered`, or `offerable`; when it is `coordinator`, `likely_admission_state` MUST be one of the SPEC-047-R001 coordinator states; `provider_guidance` MUST reuse the SPEC-046-R003 object shape and closed enums. This is the sole v0.1 dry-run schema; it is not a submission receipt, admission status response, catalog-economics row, or legacy `models_browse.v1` row, and v0.1 decoders MUST reject unknown fields before treating the result as actionable. Offer submission MAY omit the evaluation digest only when the dry-run response explicitly labels the offer as more likely to be rejected or confined to non-earning states. The CLI MUST reserve `models admission status <candidate> --json` for provider status readback and `models admission withdraw <candidate> --json` for provider-initiated withdrawal. `models admission status <candidate> --json` MUST emit a closed JSON envelope with `schema: "model_admission_status.v1"`, `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `admission_state`, `admission_state_source`, nullable `coordinator_event_id`, nullable `state_observed_at`, `provider_guidance`, `allowed_next_states`, and `warnings`. `admission_state_source` MUST be `local_default` or `coordinator`; when it is `local_default`, `admission_state` MUST be `local_only`, `not_offered`, or `offerable`; when it is `coordinator`, `admission_state` MUST be one of the SPEC-047-R001 coordinator states. `provider_guidance` MUST reuse the SPEC-046-R003 object shape and closed enums; for status output, `provider_guidance.next_action` MUST be appropriate to the transition table and `provider_guidance.earning_path_class` MUST be `not_earning_yet_catalog_or_receipt_path_exists`, `no_earning_path_in_v0_1`, `settlement_capable`, or `local_inventory_only`. `allowed_next_states` MUST contain only states allowed by SPEC-047-R001 for coordinator-sourced states and MUST be empty for `local_default` states that have not entered coordinator admission. Revocation, rejection, sanction, withdrawal, and demotion states MUST include a non-null `provider_guidance.transition_reason_code`. The v0.1 offer package MUST be a closed schema; unknown fields MUST be rejected before persistence, state transition, probing, or routing. The v0.1 offer package MUST include schema id, provider id, candidate id, SPEC-046 discovery digest, optional SPEC-046 evaluation digest, runtime source enum, served model reference, catalog match if any, artifact/hash evidence if available, advisory capabilities, fit evidence source, local readiness, requested disclosure class, timestamp, nonce, and provider signature. It MUST NOT include raw prompts, raw completions, endpoint URLs, endpoint origins, hostnames, IP addresses, ports, Unix-domain socket paths, local file paths, raw endpoint credentials, buyer credentials, wallet secrets, or unredacted adapter error bodies. Runtime source and served model reference are identity descriptors only; they MUST NOT be interpreted as network locations for coordinator-side dereference. **[amended v0.1.5]** The `model_admission_status.v1` field set is unchanged, and one value semantic changes: `catalog_model_key` now carries only a coordinator-resolved key (the catalog match of the offer paragraph under SPEC-047-R001) and is null for an unmatched offer, so a provider assertion is never echoed as identity; `provider_guidance.earning_path_class` follows it (`no_earning_path_in_v0_1` for an unmatched offer). Provider-facing visibility of `catalog_match_state`, `catalog_match_reason`, the member set, and the bound member is a later versioned status schema (slice 6), not v1.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:136:`models admission withdraw <candidate> --json` MUST submit a closed coordinator request with `schema: "model_admission_withdraw_request.v1"` and emit the coordinator-derived response with `schema: "model_admission_withdraw.v1"`. The request MUST include `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `idempotency_key`, `nonce`, `timestamp`, `reason_code`, `signing_key_id` or `signing_key_digest`, `signature_algorithm`, and `provider_signature`; it MUST NOT include client-provided `previous_admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, or `resulting_admission_state`. `reason_code` MUST be a closed enum; v0.1 values are `provider_requested`, `wrong_model`, `runtime_unavailable`, `identity_mismatch`, `policy_uncertain`, and `other_operator_reason`. The withdrawal signature MUST use the same provider admission identity class as offers, over a canonical domain-separated preimage with domain `macprovider.model_admission.withdraw.v1`, and MUST bind `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `idempotency_key`, `nonce`, `timestamp`, and `reason_code`. Bearer-token authentication may authenticate the transport, but a bearer token alone is never the withdrawal-signing root. Payout keys, wallet private keys, buyer keys, receipt-signing keys, endpoint credentials, and local discovery namespace secrets MUST NOT sign withdrawals or appear in withdrawal payloads. The coordinator MUST reject unknown request fields, stale/unknown/bearer-only/receipt-key-only/payout-key/wallet-key/buyer-key signatures, mismatched provider/candidate/served-model tuples, withdrawals for another provider, replayed nonces, and idempotency-key reuse whose canonical request digest differs from the first request stored for that provider and candidate before appending any event. Exact idempotent retries for the same provider, candidate, idempotency key, and canonical request digest MAY return the original `model_admission_withdraw.v1` response, but MUST NOT append a second state transition or delete local model artifacts. The response MUST include `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `idempotency_key`, `reason_code`, `previous_admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, `resulting_admission_state`, `provider_guidance`, and `warnings`; the coordinator MUST derive previous state, event id, acceptance timestamp, and resulting state atomically from durable coordinator state. A later re-entry from `withdrawn` MUST use a fresh provider-signed offer with refreshed evidence digests.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:138:The v0.1 offer package MUST be a closed schema; unknown fields MUST be rejected before persistence, state transition, probing, or routing. The v0.1 offer package MUST include schema id, provider id, candidate id, SPEC-046 discovery digest, optional SPEC-046 evaluation digest, runtime source enum, served model reference, catalog match if any under the SPEC-047-R001 `catalog_matched` definition, artifact/hash evidence if available, advisory capabilities, fit evidence source, local readiness, requested disclosure class, timestamp, nonce, signing key id or digest, provider signature, and signature algorithm. The signing key MUST be the provider's CLI-owned Ed25519 admission identity accepted through SPEC-001/SPEC-026 as the coordinator-authoritative current `provider_admission_public_key` for that `provider_id` at mutation time. Pending or recovery keys qualify for mutating BYOM offers or withdrawals only after the SPEC-026 compare-and-swap or recovery transaction has succeeded and the coordinator now identifies that key as the current admission key. Previous keys are valid only for the rollback/readback compatibility role explicitly allowed by SPEC-026 and MUST NOT authorize mutating BYOM offer or withdrawal requests. The signed payload MUST bind `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, discovery digest, optional evaluation digest, timestamp, nonce/idempotency key, requested disclosure class, and catalog/hash evidence. Bearer-token authentication may be required to authenticate the transport, but a bearer token alone is never the offer-signing root. Payout keys, wallet private keys, buyer keys, receipt-signing keys, endpoint credentials, and local discovery namespace secrets MUST NOT sign BYOM offers or appear in offer payloads. It MUST NOT include raw prompts, raw completions, endpoint URLs, endpoint origins, hostnames, IP addresses, ports, Unix-domain socket paths, local file paths, raw endpoint credentials, buyer credentials, wallet secrets, payout secrets, or unredacted adapter error bodies. Runtime source and served model reference are identity descriptors only; they MUST NOT be interpreted as network locations for coordinator-side dereference.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:142:**[amended v0.1.5]** An operator decision (SPEC-047-R001) to `catalog_priced` or `settlement_capable` MUST fail closed — appending nothing, answering with the clause's code — unless, evaluated inside the provider's decision critical section (SPEC-047-R001; one section per `provider_id`) at decision time (and, for the dual-control `settlement_capable` edge, again at approval time): (i) the candidate's latest offer event carries `catalog_match_state` = `catalog_matched` (`catalog_match_required` otherwise), and every recorded member still resolves in the CURRENT release: a `candidate_row` member's row tuple (`catalog_model_key`, `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256`) is present in the current candidate catalog, and an `artifact_feed` member resolves in the current identity set to the same (`catalog_model_key`, `artifact_id`, pair) — provenance MAY differ (a re-stamp) and the decision records the CURRENT provenance; any member that no longer resolves is `catalog_match_stale` (a content change requires a fresh offer; evidence is never repaired); (ii) that row's `runtime_status` is `recommendable` in the current candidate catalog (`catalog_row_not_recommendable` for a `listed`, `candidate`, or `blocked` row — a removed row already failed (i); SPEC-023 AC-CAT-7(iii)), and every recorded member still allows the recorded `runtime_source` (`runtime_source_not_allowed` otherwise); the coordinator stamps the row's status on every bound session as `catalog_row_status` and refreshes it in the R006(c) sweep, and the buyer re-reads it at route time as defence in depth (redundant by construction, since a change is also a linearized revocation); (iii) trusted Tier-2 catalog material exists for that row (`catalog_material_unavailable` otherwise), and the decision event binds `catalog_id`, `catalog_body_digest`, `catalog_signature_key_id`, `catalog_signature_pubkey_fingerprint` from it and `catalog_model_key` = the resolved key — that material is proof of the ROW binding (catalog identity, body digest, signer, and the row's own `model_sha256`, the primary member) and the pricing key; for an `artifact_feed` member it is never proof of the member's hash, which is proven only by the member's six values (SPEC-010-R004 v1.8, R007(d)); the binding is that composite and an implementation MUST NOT read the row material's digest as the member's expected hash; (iv) for `settlement_capable` only, the provider's live session — the registry keeps exactly ONE active session per provider id; a new hello replaces the previous session and re-derives its binding — MUST be bound to this candidate (below), admitted on the current release or on a retained compatible-previous release whose catalog carries the same row tuple, with a SPEC-010 identity verdict that is `hash_verified` and pinned (SPEC-010-R007(b)/(c) session authority) for a pair that is one of the recorded members admissible for the recorded `runtime_source` (the serving path a session presents is that source; a session can present only `mlx_cache` and only an `mlx_safetensors` member can bind — **[amended v0.1.10]** a loopback source never binds, per the loopback settlement bar below), resolved in the identity set of the session's OWN admitted release (SPEC-010-R004 v1.8: the coordinator retains the identity set of each compatible-previous release it retains), and with its SPEC-022 receipt key present; no such session is `no_verified_session`. The decision event then binds THAT member as the settlement identity: `expected_catalog_model_hash` / `_algorithm` = its pair and, for an `artifact_feed` member, the six SPEC-047-R003 values of the session's binding (the provenance of the release the session resolved in); a `candidate_row` member binds the row directly and carries none. A `catalog_priced` decision binds the key and the member set, not a served member. **Session-to-candidate binding** is coordinator-derived, never provider-asserted: at hello (initial or replacement) and whenever an event is appended for a provider's candidate, the coordinator binds the session to the candidate whose latest non-terminal event (`offer_submitted` through `settlement_capable`) is `catalog_matched` on the row whose `model_id` the session serves; zero candidates bind nothing (an unmatched candidate never binds, so the non-BYOM session path applies) and two or more bind nothing, the coordinator logs `ambiguous_candidates`, and R006(a) then treats the affected `catalog_priced`/`settlement_capable` candidates as identity drift (the session no longer verifies for a bound candidate). The binding is `candidate_id`, `catalog_model_key`, the candidate's current `coordinator_event_id`, and `catalog_row_status`; it is refreshed on every event appended for that candidate (a revocation refreshes it to the terminal event and thereby clears routability), cleared on withdrawal, model change, and disconnect, and re-derived at the next hello; every binding mutation takes the provider's section. Buyer default routing and settlement MUST require a session binding whose `coordinator_event_id` equals the candidate's latest event and whose state is `settlement_capable`, MUST compare the session's verified pair (and `artifact_id`, for a feed member) to the decision's bound member by CONTENT, and MUST create and persist the BYOM route-time snapshot by the compare-and-insert of SPEC-047-R001 (re-reading head, binding, and release generation immediately before the insert), recording the session's CURRENT binding provenance; served-model-name or asserted-key lookups are never a fallback.
specs/SPEC-006-buyer-api.md:1724:`X-MacProvider-Internal-Conv` is an internal deployment header, not a buyer API header. The coordinator's externally reachable nginx vhost, proxy layer, or equivalent edge boundary MUST strip `X-MacProvider-Internal-Conv` and any other `X-MacProvider-Internal-*` header from every path that could be reached outside the gateway. The coordinator MUST treat `X-MacProvider-Internal-Conv` as valid only on authenticated or network-restricted gateway-originated traffic; it MUST NEVER accept this header from direct buyer traffic. A deployment where buyer-reachable requests can supply or preserve this header is non-compliant with SPEC-006 v0.8 and SPEC-004 v0.2.

specs/SPEC-041-relay-blind-request-encryption.md:72:Gateway, coordinator, provider runtime, and buyer tooling MUST each default relay-blind support off. A required request succeeds only when every component is enabled, the assigned live provider/session has fresh authenticated key evidence, and all durable stores are available and fresh. specs/SPEC-003-open-onboarding.md:75:**Change log v0.8.3 (PR #78, merged 2026-06-12):** Post-deploy hardening from the 2026-06-12 first end-to-end M0-5/M1-6 production deploy on Pearl. FR-C9.4 amended with the unused-token self-heal clause. When the active row in `provider_tokens` for a `provider_id` has `last_used_at IS NULL` AND a tokenless connect arrives, the coordinator MUST revoke that row and mint a fresh token for the incoming connect, instead of rejecting. A token that has never authenticated cannot have been captured-and-used by an attacker — the codex MAJOR-1 credential-capture vector that v0.8.1 closed requires the attacker to have authenticated at least once, which sets `last_used_at`. The strict-reject path is preserved for `last_used_at IS NOT NULL` (a used token is a live credential and the security argument applies in full). The trigger was the 2026-06-12 deploy gap: `air5` connected to the v1.3.0 coordinator under `require_provider_tokens=false`, the coordinator restarted to v1.3.1-5 and minted a self-serve token during admission, but `air5`'s old binary did not consume the ack-frame's `assigned_provider_token`. On reconnect the binary sent tokenless and v0.8.2's strict TOFU rejected it indefinitely. With v0.8.3, the same sequence revokes-and-remints automatically and the provider re-enters the pool with a fresh row. Storage-layer primitive added: `auth.Store.RevokeUnusedTokenForProvider(ctx, providerID) (revoked bool, err error)` performs the conditional revoke as a single-statement `UPDATE` which SQLite WAL serializes against concurrent writers. v0.8.4 supersedes by composing this with the PR #69 quarantine primitive.

specs/SPEC-002-coordinator.md:1922:**Deploy ordering (v1.5.0).** Coordinator MUST be deployed first; it accepts and persists `X-MacProvider-Account` whether or not the gateway sends it. Gateway then deploys with the unconditional header. Auditor tooling MUST detect the boundary at row granularity (not schema granularity): rows with NULL `account_id` are either (a) pre-v1.5.0-coordinator rows, (b) v1.5.0-coordinator rows from a pre-v0.9.1 gateway, or (c) v1.5.0-coordinator rows written during a v1.4.x rollback window where the column existed but the writer didn't populate it. In all three cases the join MUST fall back to the prior `external_request_id`-only key and accept the documented ambiguity. Tooling MUST NOT use `PRAGMA table_info(request_log)` column-presence as a switch — that would misclassify rollback-window rows as scoped-ready. Use `account_id IS NOT NULL` as the per-row gate instead.

specs/SPEC-023-installer-autotune-recommend.md:916:§12.2 records the #813 forward-incompatibility trap. The deployed CLI Swift strict decoder enumerates the exact allowed candidate-row keys (`model_id`, `model_revision`, `model_sha256`, `min_ram_gb`, `min_bandwidth_tier`, `bench_gate`, `runtime_status`, `notes`, `draft_candidates`, `workload_profiles`) and throws on any other key; the release generator and the coordinator feed validators enforce the same closed set. Publishing an artifact set as a new candidate-row field would therefore fail-close every deployed provider — integrity failure on the whole catalog, blocking autoupdate and coordinator join — which is the exact failure the oMLX activation gate exists to prevent.
specs/SPEC-023-installer-autotune-recommend.md:1035:- **Which artifacts are identity members is SPEC-010's decision; which runtime sources may settle is SPEC-047-R003(iv)'s (v0.14.3).** In v0.10.0–v0.10.2 SPEC-010 v1.6 recognized exactly one identity per model key (the row's `model_sha256`), so only the artifact named by `primary_artifact_id` could reach `catalog_priced` or `settlement_capable`, be reported as the SPEC-010 wire pair, or bind a SPEC-022 route-time snapshot. SPEC-010 v1.7 **R007** recognizes every `verified` artifact of the release-bound feed as a member of the key's identity set — `macprovider.gguf-file.v1` is a canonical pair from v1.7 — so from v0.10.3 a non-primary artifact of either format may do all three when the R007 conditions hold (exact pair match, single resolution, six-value route-time evidence for every feed-derived binding). **(v0.14.3)** Identity is not settlement for loopback runtimes: every `gguf` artifact's sources are loopback (matrix above), and SPEC-047-R003(iv) v0.1.10 bars every loopback `runtime_source` from `settlement_capable` until a later SPEC-047-R003 amendment names a coordinator-recorded trust binding and a trusted usage source. Until then only an `mlx_safetensors` artifact served by `mlx_cache` can settle, and a `gguf` artifact's R007 identity reaches at most `catalog_priced`. Every gate in this SPEC — `recommendable` for paid defaults, `listed` as unpriced intake, §5, §12 — is unchanged; the widening is one of identity, not of tier.

docs/product-roadmap/build-1/reservation-rebaseline-plan-v15.md:247:2. The direct cancel process acquires `failure.lock` and then `cancel.lock`. Immediately before the first `failure.lock` attempt it records `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW`; both acquisitions, including spurious wakeups and retries, share one total deadline exactly 2.000 seconds later. If both locks are not held while elapsed time remains strictly less than 2.000 seconds, the process releases either acquired lock plus every waiter/descriptor/resource, emits the valid `busy` acknowledgement described below, and exits without reading or mutating marker, active/history, terminal, cleanup-phase, temp, artifact, or operation state. Once both are held, that instant is the cancellation decision linearization point. The process validates the bounded active/pending/history/terminal projection needed for the total predicate, and may read/reuse the single exact marker record, durably remove only a validated marker bound to an older attempt, and durably create/readback-validate only the requested current-attempt marker. It never touches any other marker, repairs or compacts history, recovers state, renames or deletes a target, or acquires `operation.lock`, a cleanup lock, `RecommendationAdoptionLock`, the control socket, or runtime reservation. It releases `cancel.lock` then `failure.lock` and emits no event. A busy operation lock never authorizes cancel-side recovery mutation.

The @Augustas11-owned finalized authority commit is exactly `922624a7959253aae0581c6e2db22f827925072b`, and its SPEC-001 v1.9.17/SPEC-044 v0.2.8 bytes freeze exact catalog-economics read/run/cancel spelling; the v1 trio `model_catalog_economics_v1` / `models catalog-economics.v1` / `model_catalog_economics.v1` and analogous v2 trio; selection capability placement in manifest `local_status_capabilities`; command-token and schema-companion placement in manifest `command_schemas`; the complete trio in flat fresh local status; the existing local-status/control-frame tier prerequisites; schema-companion-alone non-selection; support for separate valid v1/v2 manifest tiers; reserved-prefix-scoped unknown rejection and unrelated-value tolerance; static-card/no-indicator/no-retry/no-call behavior for no supported trio and every removal/reserved-addition/misplacement/dual/mixed/unknown-reserved/stale/conflict/manifest-status negative; current manifest/current v1 status, new Malibu/old v1 CLI, current Malibu/new v2-only CLI fallback, and new v2 manifest/status upgrade orders; exact `model catalog unavailable`/`projection_unavailable` warning and retry only after a negotiated request fails, times out, or returns a malformed envelope; and the constructive pre-work lifecycle with immutable-action validation, a prospective fresh attempt, one total 2.000-second failure→cancel deadline before semantic and cancel-visible checks, exactly one nonblocking operation-lock attempt, operation-conflict reacquisition within the remaining original deadline, and a new total 2.000-second operation→failure→cancel deadline after successful nonblocking operation acquisition. Missing either required lock yields the exact UTF-8 stderr line `{"error_code":"dispatch_state_busy"}` plus LF, empty stdout, no event, exit 5, and no mutation; semantic failure creates one exact closed pending `failed_dispatch`, releases every lock before its sequence-1 event, and exits 3 without reacquisition, while the next failure writer or startup recovery performs copy-before-delete compaction under its ordered lock set. The same authority freezes the exhaustive lock graph: projection publication, active creation, non-cleanup final marker check and commit, ordinary terminal/history mutation, and startup/recovery use operation→failure→cancel; failed-dispatch creation/compaction/eviction and every direct-cancel-visible read use failure→cancel; direct cancel uses that pair under one total 2.000-second deadline and may mutate only the exact marker; live periodic marker polling is the sole operation→cancel path and is bounded read-only; cleanup mutation uses operation→cleanup→cancel, releases cleanup after durable cleanup state, and only then may use operation→failure→cancel for terminal/history work; adoption uses operation→adoption→socket→runtime. No cleanup/failure overlap, reverse edge, post-event reacquisition, or unbounded fairness claim is permitted. Pending/history movement publishes and readback-validates replacement history before pending unlink, tolerates crash duplicates through identity deduplication, and leaves no durable gap; a terminal failed dispatch present at direct-cancel pair-acquisition linearization always returns exact `terminal`. The authority also retains the exact catalog-only `unavailable`/`none`/`local_default:not_offered` null/false/no-action sentinel placed only in exact R008 `Blocked` with `Network catalog`/`Current`/`Ready`/`Needs preparation` one-fault negatives, cross-candidate rejection, and candidate-associated all-non-null verbatim guidance binding; coordinator no-event/event-backed `not_offered` plus exact source-aware local-default/coordinator English meanings and localization/accessibility/source-swap negatives; exact **Eligible to earn on qualifying settled requests** conditional copy and no current-income claim; exact admission-only `local_only` copy with independent readiness/usability evidence; the exact 12-state admission inventory; event codes and total precedence; exhaustive R002/R003 eligibility including `verification_status: verified`; worker-only sequencing; six-outcome cancellation acknowledgement with exact echo/nullability/exit/mutation/resource rules; bounded complete cleanup targets with target-level immutable `event_model_key`, public v2 action copies that reject `event_model_key` and bind only the enclosing digest/size, RFC 8785 equality between action copies, target/receipt/private-reservation event-key mismatch negatives, orphan event-correlation proof, and separate/equal-two-copy mutation proofs; authenticated root locator/identity and already-open unpublished owner-only temp/empty-ACL-before-sensitive-byte/revalidation rules; the exact SPEC-044-R005 total ranking tuple with null order/tagged length-prefixed canonical identity/duplicate-canonical-identity rejection and nontrusted components 2-6 null; app-owned refresh generation and constant-space transport/backpressure; logical-byte accounting and truthful APFS copy; exact budgets/configuration precedence; and published/staging continuous final-check-through-durable-readback-validated-`tombstoned` cleanup semantics.
docs/product-roadmap/build-1/reservation-rebaseline-plan-v14.md:244:2. The direct cancel process acquires `failure.lock` and then `cancel.lock`. Immediately before the first `failure.lock` attempt it records `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW`; both acquisitions, including spurious wakeups and retries, share one total deadline exactly 2.000 seconds later. If both locks are not held while elapsed time remains strictly less than 2.000 seconds, the process releases either acquired lock plus every waiter/descriptor/resource, emits the valid `busy` acknowledgement described below, and exits without reading or mutating marker, active/history, terminal, cleanup-phase, temp, artifact, or operation state. Once both are held, that instant is the cancellation decision linearization point. The process validates the bounded active/pending/history/terminal projection needed for the total predicate, and may read/reuse the single exact marker record, durably remove only a validated marker bound to an older attempt, and durably create/readback-validate only the requested current-attempt marker. It never touches any other marker, repairs or compacts history, recovers state, renames or deletes a target, or acquires `operation.lock`, a cleanup lock, `RecommendationAdoptionLock`, the control socket, or runtime reservation. It releases `cancel.lock` then `failure.lock` and emits no event. A busy operation lock never authorizes cancel-side recovery mutation.

docs/releases/coordinator-release-train.md:94:**2026-09-25 v1.8.194 apply (partial).** The signed updater applied the v1.8.194 binary pair at 03:05Z (`rollout_completed success`; updater reinstalled from the tag first). The full `deploy-pearl-vps.sh` at 03:22Z reached `compare-live` = `descends` with 0 uncovered providers, then failed its SPEC-023 exact-byte canary and **rolled back** at about 03:35Z. There was about 30 s of public 502 during the rollback restart. Why: the canary Mac `mp-26592d…` runs CLI 1.8.123. Its `~/macprovider/catalog-release` holds the Sep 8 baked `published-2026-09-02-gpt-oss-120b-v1` files, and only a signed CLI payload writes that directory, so no restart can make it byte-equal to the new release. Live now: coordinator/gateway v1.8.194 binary, catalog still `published-2026-09-23-tier2-buyer-closure-v1`. `stats-inventory-sync` is left stopped by the rollback: #1738 migration 030 is applied and the old sidecar is held. Recover per the coordinator-deploy-recover runbook. #1735 catalog activation still needs a canary whose installed CLI payload carries `published-2026-09-25-artifact-hash-correction-v1`. Fleet impact of the attempt: the new catalog was live 03:31:04–03:35:11Z. Coordinator-sourced providers picked it up, and after the rollback the Studio mp-5aad… was closed 3 times with `4001 catalog_incompatible` (03:35:51–03:37:27Z) until it refetched the old release. No closes after 03:37:40Z. By 03:45Z all 5 providers were back and `current` on `published-2026-09-23-tier2-buyer-closure-v1`, with no model-admission revocations. A rolled-back activation therefore briefly kicks every provider that fetched the new release. Providers load the coordinator's live signed catalog, and a baked catalog is only a fallback, so a CLI carrying a newer baked catalog advertises whatever Pearl serves.
docs/releases/coordinator-release-train.md:141:| Pricing corrections through the catalog-content lane (SPEC-005-R013, SPEC-023-R018, SPEC-006-R008 amended). Coordinator: request billing table and served signed rate card switch under one economics lock (release lock → economics lock → feed lock), prices resolved once before the billing write context; `--validate-autotune-release` gains `--expect-base-equivalent` and `--resolve-model-names` plus `rate_table_sha256` / `signed_rate_card_sha256` verdict fields; applied-config record gains `rate_table_sha256`, `signed_rate_card_sha256`, `autotune_release_id`, `billing_snapshot_id`. **Wholesale statements change**: each request is priced at the generation it was recorded under (uncapped aggregate math), so a model-month above 10M tokens is no longer zeroed — affected partner statements go **up**; a period with no billing snapshot now fails closed. Lane tooling that deploy ships: `scripts/catalog-release.py` (splice / extract / effective-price diff / gate), new `acknowledged-pricing-moves.json`; still to land in the same PR: journal + pre-start recovery + post-start closer units, the one-writer guard on every live-config writer, lane preflight/evidence/rollback. **Enabling rollout is two steps from the same tag, in order**: (1) reinstall the Pearl updater bundle (`install-pearl-updater.sh`: guard-bearing updater, Tier-2 watchdog, Python guard module), then (2) a full `deploy-pearl-vps.sh` (new units, recovery helper, shell guard, verifier bundle) — never a binary swap. Pricing preflight hashes every installed writer against the commit, so a deploy without step 1 stays NO_GO. Procedure: `catalog-release-decision-tree.md` §Enabling rollout. Afterwards rows-only pricing needs no coordinator release. Plan (approved 0C/0H/0M): [#1693 comment](https://github.com/Augustas11/macprovider/issues/1693#issuecomment-5800624020) | in progress (draft; merge gated on the e2e fake-Pearl run) | #1732 (#1693) |

docs/product-roadmap/build-1/reservation-rebaseline-plan-v16.md:247:2. The direct cancel process acquires `failure.lock` and then `cancel.lock`. Immediately before the first `failure.lock` attempt it records `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW`; both acquisitions, including spurious wakeups and retries, share one total deadline exactly 2.000 seconds later. If both locks are not held while elapsed time remains strictly less than 2.000 seconds, the process releases either acquired lock plus every waiter/descriptor/resource, emits the valid `busy` acknowledgement described below, and exits without reading or mutating marker, active/history, terminal, cleanup-phase, temp, artifact, or operation state. Once both are held, that instant is the cancellation decision linearization point. The process validates the bounded active/pending/history/terminal projection needed for the total predicate, and may read/reuse the single exact marker record, durably remove only a validated marker bound to an older attempt, and durably create/readback-validate only the requested current-attempt marker. It never touches any other marker, repairs or compacts history, recovers state, renames or deletes a target, or acquires `operation.lock`, a cleanup lock, `RecommendationAdoptionLock`, the control socket, or runtime reservation. It releases `cancel.lock` then `failure.lock` and emits no event. A busy operation lock never authorizes cancel-side recovery mutation.

docs/product-roadmap/build-1/reservation-rebaseline-plan-v12.md:233:Pending failed-dispatch records and ordinary terminal history share one global 256-record limit and one aggregate 262144-byte cap. Under `failure.lock`, a new failure first compacts any earlier complete pending record and applies the same deterministic oldest-terminal eviction, then creates one pending record; at most one pending record exists. The failure-only path never acquires `operation.lock`, `cancel.lock`, a cleanup lock, `RecommendationAdoptionLock`, the runtime reservation, or the serving socket, and never waits for any of them while holding `failure.lock`. A normal or startup recovery compactor takes operation→failure; a failure worker may compact its own record under `failure.lock` alone and never then acquires `operation.lock`.

docs/spec-history/spec-016/SPEC-016-IMPL-FULL-arch-r2-audit.md:51:Runtime and deploy-gate RPC URL constraints are split in an audit-stable way. Runtime validation is the trust root: `Validate` calls `validatePayoutRPCURL` for both URLs and enforces distinct hostnames at `phase4-coordinator/internal/config/config.go:1069`. The helper rejects non-HTTPS, userinfo, and literal internal/loopback/link-local/unspecified IPs at `config.go:1280`. The deploy gate mirrors those obvious checks as defense-in-depth and explicitly documents that hostname trust is deferred to TLS/SPKI at `phase4-coordinator/dist/check-deploy-config.sh:358`. Env-indirected values are resolved by runtime config loading at `config.go:737`, and the deploy gate defers unresolved env references back to runtime at `check-deploy-config.sh:333`.

   244	_coordinator_release_tag_version() {
   245	  local module_dir="$1" repo_root candidates count dirty_state tag head rows tag_object peeled_count peeled_commit tag_type verify_output remote_url
   246	  local release_tag_remote="origin"
   247	  local release_tag_remote_url="https://github.com/Augustas11/macprovider.git"
   248	  local release_tag_signer_line='Good "git" signature for augstar@gmail.com with ED25519 key SHA256:6DgoKNaOgF5c7NPHTAbNxJ2LT0uuj8U/3zObOOZjRiA'
   249	  repo_root="$(git -C "$module_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
   250	  dirty_state="$(git -C "$repo_root" status --porcelain)"
   251	  if [ -n "$dirty_state" ]; then
   252	    echo "aborting deploy: coordinator production deploy requires a clean release-tag checkout" >&2
   253	    git -C "$repo_root" status --short >&2
   254	    return 1
   255	  fi
   256	  candidates="$(git -C "$repo_root" tag --points-at HEAD | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' || true)"
   257	  count="$(printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   258	  case "$count" in
   259	    1)
   260	      tag="$candidates"
   261	      ;;
   262	    0)
   263	      echo "aborting deploy: HEAD is not exactly a numeric release tag (vX.Y.Z)" >&2
   264	      echo "  Deploy the signed coordinator/gateway release tag first; do not let git describe from main become production version authority." >&2
   265	      return 1
   266	      ;;
   267	    *)
   268	      echo "aborting deploy: HEAD has multiple numeric release tags:" >&2
   269	      printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | sed 's/^/  - /' >&2
   270	      return 1
   271	      ;;
   272	  esac
   273	  tag_type="$(git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -t "$tag" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   274	  if [ "$tag_type" != tag ]; then
   275	    echo "aborting deploy: $tag is not an annotated signed release tag" >&2
   276	    return 1
   277	  fi
   278	  if ! verify_output="$(git -C "$repo_root" verify-tag "$tag" 2>&1)"; then
   279	    echo "aborting deploy: $tag does not verify as a trusted signed tag" >&2
   280	    return 1
   281	  fi
   282	  if ! printf '%s\n' "$verify_output" | grep -qxF "$release_tag_signer_line"; then
   283	    echo "aborting deploy: $tag was signed by an unauthorized release signer" >&2
   284	    return 1
   285	  fi
   286	  remote_url="$(git -C "$repo_root" remote get-url "$release_tag_remote" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   287	  case "$remote_url" in
   288	    https://github.com/Augustas11/macprovider.git|git@github.com:Augustas11/macprovider.git|ssh://git@github.com/Augustas11/macprovider.git) ;;
   289	    *)
   290	      echo "aborting deploy: $release_tag_remote must point at the canonical Augustas11/macprovider GitHub repository" >&2
   291	      return 1
   292	      ;;
   293	  esac
   294	  head="$(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse HEAD)"
   295	  rows="$(git -C "$repo_root" ls-remote "$release_tag_remote_url" "refs/tags/$tag" "refs/tags/$tag^{}")"
   296	  tag_object="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -v ref="refs/tags/$tag" '$2 == ref { print $1 }')"
   297	  peeled_commit="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -v ref="refs/tags/$tag^{}" '$2 == ref { print $1 }')"
   298	  peeled_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$peeled_commit" | awk 'NF { count++ } END { print count + 0 }')"
   299	  if [ -z "$tag_object" ] || [ "$peeled_count" != 1 ] || [ "$peeled_commit" != "$head" ]; then
   300	    echo "aborting deploy: $tag is not the protected remote annotated tag for HEAD on $release_tag_remote" >&2
   301	    return 1
   302	  fi
   303	  printf '%s %s\n' "$tag" "$head"
   304	}

   306	_coordinator_verify_deployed_version() {
   307	  local healthz_body="$1" expected_version="$2" deployed_version
   308	  deployed_version=$(printf '%s' "$healthz_body" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('version', '?'))" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
   309	  if [ "$deployed_version" = "?" ]; then
   310	    echo "  CRITICAL provenance MISSING: /healthz returned no \"version\" field" >&2
   311	    echo "           This almost certainly means the deployed binary predates the" >&2
   312	    echo "           M0-5 instrumentation (PR #18) and the rollback gate is bypassed." >&2
   313	    echo "           Expected was: $expected_version" >&2
   314	    echo "           See audits/2026-06-10/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURE.md to replace the live binary." >&2
   315	    return 7
   316	  elif [ "$deployed_version" = "$expected_version" ]; then
   317	    echo "  provenance OK: deployed=$deployed_version | expected=$expected_version"
   318	  else
   319	    echo "  aborting deploy: provenance mismatch: deployed=$deployed_version | expected=$expected_version" >&2
   320	    echo "       (deployed binary does not match the exact local release tag — rollback before commit)" >&2
   321	    return 8
   322	  fi
   323	}

   363	def open_dir_at(parent_fd, name, label):
   364	    try:
   365	        fd = os.open(name, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=parent_fd)
   366	    except OSError as exc:
   367	        die(f"cannot safely open Tier-2 migration directory {label}: {exc}")

   372	def open_file_at(parent_fd, name, label, *, absent_ok=False):
   373	    try:
   374	        fd = os.open(name, os.O_RDONLY | NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=parent_fd)
   375	    except FileNotFoundError:
   376	        if absent_ok:
   377	            return None
   378	        die(f"missing Tier-2 migration file {label}")
   379	    except OSError as exc:
   380	        if exc.errno == errno.ELOOP:
   381	            die(f"unsafe Tier-2 migration symlink: {label}")
   382	        die(f"cannot safely open Tier-2 migration file {label}: {exc}")
   383	    validate_regular_file(fd, label)
   384	    return fd

   387	def read_small_file_at(parent_fd, name, label):
   388	    fd = open_file_at(parent_fd, name, label, absent_ok=True)
   389	    if fd is None:
   390	        return None
   391	    with os.fdopen(fd, "rb", closefd=True) as handle:
   392	        value = handle.read(4096)
   393	        if handle.read(1):
   394	            die(f"unsafe Tier-2 migration state file too large: {label}")
   395	    try:
   396	        return value.decode("ascii")
   397	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
   398	        raise SystemExit(f"unsafe Tier-2 migration state file is not ASCII: {label}") from exc

   401	def compare_fd(left_fd, right_fd):
   402	    os.lseek(left_fd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
   403	    os.lseek(right_fd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
   404	    while True:
   405	        left = os.read(left_fd, 1024 * 1024)
   406	        right = os.read(right_fd, 1024 * 1024)
   407	        if left != right:
   408	            return False
   409	        if not left:
   410	            return True

   478	# symlink path) + logical `pwd`. All later artifact reads,
   479	# check-deploy-config, config uploads, and vhost templates hang
   480	# off DIST_DIR, so any parent-symlink retargeting attack that
   481	# survives helper sourcing would still land here.
   482	DIST_DIR="$_PEARL_TLS_SCRIPT_DIR"

   488	if [ "$DRY_RUN_LOCAL" != "1" ]; then
   489	  COORDINATOR_RELEASE_IDENTITY="$(_coordinator_release_tag_version "$MODULE_DIR")" || exit 2
   490	  COORDINATOR_RELEASE_VERSION="${COORDINATOR_RELEASE_IDENTITY%% *}"
   491	  COORDINATOR_RELEASE_COMMIT="${COORDINATOR_RELEASE_IDENTITY#* }"

   495	# #1688: scripts/catalog-verifier-bundle.txt is the one list of files every
   496	# shipped copy of catalog-release.py needs beside it. Entries become archive
   497	# paths and remote file names, so reject anything but plain scripts/<name>.
   498	_parse_catalog_verifier_bundle() {
   499	  _bundle_seen=" "
   500	  while IFS= read -r _bundle_line || [ -n "$_bundle_line" ]; do
   501	    case "$_bundle_line" in '#'*) continue ;; esac
   502	    if ! printf '%s\n' "$_bundle_line" | grep -Eq '^scripts/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' ||
   503	      [ "$_bundle_line" = "scripts/." ] || [ "$_bundle_line" = "scripts/.." ]; then
   504	      echo "aborting deploy: invalid catalog verifier bundle entry: '$_bundle_line'" >&2
   505	      return 1
   506	    fi
   507	    case "$_bundle_seen" in
   508	      *" $_bundle_line "*)
   509	        echo "aborting deploy: duplicate catalog verifier bundle entry: $_bundle_line" >&2
   510	        return 1
   511	        ;;
   512	    esac
   513	    _bundle_seen="$_bundle_seen$_bundle_line "
   514	    printf '%s\n' "$_bundle_line"
   515	  done
   516	  case "$_bundle_seen" in
   517	    *" scripts/catalog-release.py "*) ;;
   518	    *)
   519	      echo "aborting deploy: catalog verifier bundle must list scripts/catalog-release.py" >&2
   520	      return 1
   521	      ;;
   522	  esac
   523	}

  2874	    @staticmethod
  2875	    def _systemd_seconds(value: str) -> int:
  2876	        match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+)(us|ms|s|min|h)", value)
  2877	        if not match:
  2878	            raise UpdateError(f"unsupported systemd duration: {value!r}")
  2879	        amount = int(match.group(1))
  2880	        unit = match.group(2)
  2881	        if unit == "us":
  2882	            return amount // 1_000_000
  2883	        if unit == "ms":
  2884	            return amount // 1_000
  2885	        if unit == "s":
  2886	            return amount
  2887	        if unit == "min":
  2888	            return amount * 60
  2889	        return amount * 3600

  2897	            expected_mode = CANARY_AUTHORITY_FILE_MODES[path]
